name: electron
description: Elementary particle not affected by the strong force having a spin 1/2, a negative elementary charge and a rest mass of 0.000548579903(13) u, or 0.51099906(15) MeV.

name: vitamin A
description: Any member of a group of fat-soluble retinoids produced via metabolism of provitamin A carotenoids that exhibit biological activity against vitamin A deficiency. Vitamin A is involved in immune function, vision, reproduction, and cellular communication.

name: pyridoxal(1+)
description: A pyridinium ion obtained by protonation of the ring nitrogen of pyridoxal.

name: steroid aldehyde
description: Any steroid substituted by a formyl group.

name: Mycoplasma genitalium metabolite
description: Any bacterial metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in Mycoplasma genitalium.

name: C27-steroid
description: A steroid compound with a structure based on a 27-carbon (cholestane) skeleton.

name: EC 2.7.7.7 (DNA-directed DNA polymerase) inhibitor
description: A DNA polymerase inhibitor that interferes with the action of a DNA-directed DNA polymerase (EC 2.7.7.7).

name: dicarboxylic acids and O-substituted derivatives
description: A class of carbonyl compound encompassing dicarboxylic acids and any derivatives obtained by substitution of either one or both of the carboxy hydrogens.

name: hyaluronate
description: A carbohydrate acid derivative anion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy groups of hyaluronic acid; major species at pH 7.3.

name: 1-phenylpropan-2-amine
description: A primary amine that is isopropylamine in which a hydrogen attached to one of the methyl groups has been replaced by a phenyl group.

name: saturated dicarboxylic acid dianion(2-)
description: A carboxylic acid dianion obtained by deprotonation of both carboxy groups of any dicarboxylic acid that contains no carbon-carbon double bonds.

name: volatile organic compound
description: Any organic compound having an initial boiling point less than or equal to 250 degreeC (482 degreeF) measured at a standard atmospheric pressure of 101.3 kPa.

name: glycol
description: A diol in which the two hydroxy groups are on different carbon atoms, usually but not necessarily adjacent.

name: 3-oxo-Delta(4)-steroid group
description: An organic group derived from any 3-oxo-Delta(4)-steroid.

name: pro-agent
description: A compound that, on administration, undergoes conversion by biochemical (enzymatic), chemical (possibly following an enzymatic step), or physical (e.g. photochemical) activation processes before becoming the active agent for which it is a pro-agent.

name: acetylsalicylate
description: A benzoate that is the conjugate base of acetylsalicylic acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.

name: secondary ammonium ion
description: An organic cation obtained by protonation of any secondary amino compound; major species at pH 7.3.

name: metalloid atom
description: An atom of an element that exhibits properties that are between those of metals and nonmetals, or that has a mixture of them. The term generally includes boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony, and tellurium, while carbon, aluminium, selenium, polonium, and astatine are less commonly included.

name: tertiary ammonium ion
description: An organic cation obtained by protonation of the amino group of any tertiary amino compound.

name: endocrine disruptor
description: Any compound that can disrupt the functions of the endocrine (hormone) system

name: inorganic acid
description: A Bronsted acid derived from one or more inorganic compounds. Inorganic acids (also known as mineral acids) form hydrons and conjugate base ions when dissolved in water.

name: apoprotein
description: An apoprotein is a protein devoid of its characteristic prosthetic group or metal.

name: gas molecular entity
description: Any main group molecular entity that is gaseous at standard temperature and pressure (STP; 0degreeC and 100 kPa).

name: alpha-hydroxy ketone
description: An alpha-oxyketone that has a hydroxy group as the alpha-oxy moiety.

name: retinoid anion
description: A carboxylic acid anion obtained by deprotonation of any retinoid carboxy group.

name: primary alpha-hydroxy ketone
description: An alpha-hydroxy ketone in which the carbonyl group and the hydroxy group are linked by a -CH2 (methylene) group.

name: tertiary alpha-hydroxy ketone
description: An alpha-hydroxy ketone in which the carbonyl group and the hydroxy group are linked by a carbon bearing two organyl groups.

name: phenyl acetates
description: An acetate ester obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of acetic acid with the hydroxy group of any phenol.

name: secondary carboxamide
description: A carboxamide resulting from the formal condensation of a carboxylic acid with a primary amine; formula RC(=O)NHR(1).

name: kaolinite
description: An aluminosilicate mineral with approximate chemical composition H2Al2Si2O8.H2O. Rocks that are rich in kaolinite are known as kaolin or china clay.

name: kaolin
description: An aluminosilicate soft white mineral named after the hill in China (Kao-ling) from which it was mined for centuries. In its natural state kaolin is a white, soft powder consisting principally of the mineral kaolinite, and varying amounts of other minerals such as muscovite, quartz, feldspar, and anatase. It is used in the manufacture of china and porcelain and also widely used in the production of paper, rubber, paint, drying agents, and many other products.

name: L-tyrosinal(1+)
description: A primary ammonium ion resulting from the protonation of the amino group of L-tyrosinal.

name: 24G7 epitope
description: An antigenic epitope recognized by an anti-bilirubin monoclonal antibody designated 24G7. A substructure of bilirubin IXalpha, it is the region containing the oxo group at C-1, the methyl group at C-2, C-(4, 5, 6, 9), and N-21 and -22.

name: glutamate(1-)
description: An alpha-amino-acid anion that is the conjugate base of glutamic acid, having anionic carboxy groups and a cationic amino group

name: digoxin(1-)
description: An organic anion that is the conjugate base of digoxin resulting from the deprotonation of furanone moiety; major species at pH 7.3.

name: insulin
description: A peptide hormone which consists of two polypeptide chains, A- and B- chains which are linked together by disulfide bonds. The amino acid sequence of insulin varies across species and certain segments of the molecule are highly conserved. In most species, the A chain consists of 21 amino acids and the B chain consists of 30 amino acids. In mammals, insulin is synthesised in the pancreas within the beta cells whereas in certain species of fish, the insulin-producing tissue is uniquely located in separate structures called Brockmann bodies.

name: emetic
description: Any agent that induces nausea and vomiting.

name: D-dopa zwitterion
description: An amino acid zwitterion obtained from the transfer of a proton from the carboxy group to the amino group of D-dopa. Major microspecies at pH 7.3.

name: electron donor
description: A molecular entity that can transfer an electron to another molecular entity.

name: acceptor
description: A molecular entity that can accept an electron, a pair of electrons, an atom or a group from another molecular entity.

name: choline
description: A choline that is the parent compound of the cholines class, consisting of ethanolamine having three methyl substituents attached to the amino function.

name: acetylsalicylic acid
description: A member of the class of benzoic acids that is salicylic acid in which the hydrogen that is attached to the phenolic hydroxy group has been replaced by an acetoxy group. A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug with cyclooxygenase inhibitor activity.

name: acetic acid
description: A simple monocarboxylic acid containing two carbons.

name: water
description: An oxygen hydride consisting of an oxygen atom that is covalently bonded to two hydrogen atoms

name: squalene
description: A triterpene consisting of 2,6,10,15,19,23-hexamethyltetracosane having six double bonds at the 2-, 6-, 10-, 14-, 18- and 22-positions with (all-E)-configuration.

name: aldose
description: Aldehydic parent sugars (polyhydroxy aldehydes H[CH(OH)]nC(=O)H, n >= 2) and their intramolecular hemiacetals.

name: L-alpha-amino acid
description: Any alpha-amino acid having L-configuration at the alpha-carbon.

name: primary alcohol
description: A primary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, -OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has either three hydrogen atoms attached to it or only one other carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms attached to it.

name: formate
description: A monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of formic acid. Induces severe metabolic acidosis and ocular injury in human subjects.

name: L-dopa
description: An optically active form of dopa having L-configuration. Used to treat the stiffness, tremors, spasms, and poor muscle control of Parkinson's disease

name: malonate(2-)
description: A dicarboxylic acid dianion obtained by the deprotonation of the carboxy groups of malonic acid.

name: polypeptide
description: A peptide containing ten or more amino acid residues.

name: sterol
description: Any 3-hydroxy steroid whose skeleton is closely related to cholestan-3-ol (additional carbon atoms may be present in the side chain).

name: biotin
description: An organic heterobicyclic compound that consists of 2-oxohexahydro-1H-thieno[3,4-d]imidazole having a valeric acid substituent attached to the tetrahydrothiophene ring. The parent of the class of biotins.

name: D-glutamic acid
description: An optically active form of glutamic acid having D-configuration.

name: (R)-lactate
description: An optically active form of lactate having (R)-configuration.

name: L-glutamic acid
description: An optically active form of glutamic acid having L-configuration.

name: halide anion
description: A monoatomic monoanion resulting from the addition of an electron to any halogen atom.

name: cholesterol
description: A cholestanoid consisting of cholestane having a double bond at the 5,6-position as well as a 3beta-hydroxy group.

name: ammonia
description: An azane that consists of a single nitrogen atom covelently bonded to three hydrogen atoms.

name: chondroitin D-glucuronate
description: A mucopolysaccharide composed of repeating beta-D-glucopyranuronosyl-(1->3)-beta-D-N-acetylgalactosaminyl units.

name: benzoate
description: The simplest member of the class of  benzoates that is the conjugate base of benzoic acid, comprising a benzoic acid core with a proton missing to give a charge of -1.

name: sulfate
description: A sulfur oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of both OH groups of sulfuric acid.

name: urea
description: A carbonyl group with two C-bound amine groups. The commercially available fertilizer has an analysis of 46-0-0 (N-P2O5-K2O).

name: phospholipid
description: A lipid containing phosphoric acid as a mono- or di-ester. The term encompasses phosphatidic acids and phosphoglycerides.

name: haloacetic acid
description: A monocarboxylic acid that is acetic acid in which one of the methyl hydrogens has been replaced by a halogen atom.

name: barbituric acid
description: A barbiturate, the structure of which is that of perhydropyrimidine substituted at C-2, -4 and -6 by oxo groups.  Barbituric acid is the parent compound of barbiturate drugs, although it is not itself pharmacologically active.

name: hyaluronic acid
description: A mucopolysaccharide composed of N-acetylglucosamine and glucuronic acid subunits. It is found in the connective tissues of vertebrates. A principal constituent of the extracellular matrix (ECM), it mediates the growth and metastasis of tumour cells.

name: sphingosine
description: A sphing-4-enine in which the double bond is trans.

name: carbon dioxide
description: A one-carbon compound with formula CO2 in which the carbon is attached to each oxygen atom by a double bond. A colourless, odourless gas under normal conditions, it is produced during respiration by all animals, fungi and microorganisms that depend directly or indirectly on living or decaying plants for food.

name: protein polypeptide chain
description: A naturally occurring polypeptide synthesized at the ribosome.

name: carbohydrate
description: Any member of the class of organooxygen compounds that is a polyhydroxy-aldehyde or -ketone or a lactol resulting from their intramolecular condensation (monosaccharides); substances derived from these by reduction of the carbonyl group (alditols), by oxidation of one or more hydroxy groups to afford the corresponding aldehydes, ketones, or carboxylic acids, or by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by a hydrogen atom; and polymeric products arising by intermolecular acetal formation between two or more such molecules (disaccharides, polysaccharides and oligosaccharides). Carbohydrates contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms; prior to any oxidation or reduction, most have the empirical formula Cm(H2O)n. Compounds obtained from carbohydrates by substitution, etc., are known as carbohydrate derivatives and may contain other elements. Cyclitols are generally not regarded as carbohydrates.

name: (S)-lactate
description: An optically active form of lactate having (S)-configuration.

name: peptide
description: Amide derived from two or more amino carboxylic acid molecules (the same or different) by formation of a covalent bond from the carbonyl carbon of one to the nitrogen atom of another with formal loss of water. The term is usually applied to structures formed from alpha-amino acids, but it includes those derived from any amino carboxylic acid. X = OH, OR, NH2, NHR, etc.

name: 6-aminopenicillanic acid
description: A penicillanic acid compound having a (6R)-amino substituent. The active nucleus common to all penicillins, it may be substituted at the 6-amino position to form the semisynthetic penicillins, resulting in a variety of antibacterial and pharmacologic characteristics.

name: pyridoxine
description: A hydroxymethylpyridine with hydroxymethyl groups at positions 4 and 5, a hydroxy group at position 3 and a methyl group at position 2. The 4-methanol form of vitamin B6, it is converted intoto pyridoxal phosphate which is a coenzyme for synthesis of amino acids, neurotransmitters, sphingolipids and aminolevulinic acid.

name: benzene
description: A six-carbon aromatic annulene in which each carbon atom donates one of its two 2p electrons into a delocalised pi system. A toxic, flammable liquid byproduct of coal distillation, it is used as an industrial solvent. Benzene is a carcinogen that also damages bone marrow and the central nervous system.

name: glycan
description: Any oligosaccharide, polysaccharide or their derivatives consisting of monosaccharides or monosaccharide derivatives linked by glycosidic bonds. See also http://www.ontobee.org/ontology/GNO?iri=http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GNO_00000001.

name: corticosterone
description: A 21-hydroxy steroid that consists of pregn-4-ene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 11 and 21 and oxo groups at positions 3 and 20. Corticosterone is a 21-carbon steroid hormone of the corticosteroid type produced in the cortex of the adrenal glands.

name: formaldehyde
description: An aldehyde resulting from the formal oxidation of methanol.

name: psychosine
description: A glycosylsphingoid consisting of sphingosine having a beta-D-galactosyl residue attached at the 1-position.

name: salicylic acid
description: A monohydroxybenzoic acid that is benzoic acid with a hydroxy group at the ortho position. It is obtained from the bark of the white willow and wintergreen leaves.

name: bilirubin IXalpha
description: A member of the class of  biladienes that is a linear tetrapyrrole with the dipyrrole units being of both exovinyl and endovinyl type. A product of heme degradation, it is produced in the reticuloendothelial system by the reduction of biliverdin and transported to the liver as a complex with serum albumin.

name: D-phenylalanine
description: The D-enantiomer of phenylalanine.

name: riboflavin
description: D-Ribitol in which the hydroxy group at position 5 is substituted by a 7,8-dimethyl-2,4-dioxo-3,4-dihydrobenzo[g]pteridin-10(2H)-yl moiety. It is a nutritional factor found in milk, eggs, malted barley, liver, kidney, heart, and leafy vegetables, but the richest natural source is yeast. The free form occurs only in the retina of the eye, in whey, and in urine; its principal forms in tissues and cells are as flavin mononucleotide and flavin-adenine dinucleotide.

name: ketone
description: A compound in which a carbonyl group is bonded to two carbon atoms: R2C=O (neither R may be H).

name: glycoprotein
description: A compound in which a carbohydrate component is covalently bound to a protein component.

name: 3beta-hydroxy-Delta(5)-steroid
description: Any 3beta-hydroxy-steroid that contains a double bond between positions 5 and 6.

name: glucose
description: An aldohexose used as a source of energy and metabolic intermediate.

name: carbon monoxide
description: A one-carbon compound in which the carbon is joined only to a single oxygen. It is a colourless, odourless, tasteless, toxic gas.

name: propionate
description: The conjugate base of propionic acid; a key precursor in lipid biosynthesis.

name: L-phenylalanine
description: The L-enantiomer of phenylalanine.

name: ferroptosis inducer
description: Any substance that induces or promotes ferroptosis (a type of programmed cell death dependent on iron and characterized by the accumulation of lipid peroxides) in organisms.

name: pyridoxal
description: A pyridinecarbaldehyde that is pyridine-4-carbaldehyde bearing methyl, hydroxy and hydroxymethyl substituents at positions 2, 3 and 5 respectively. The 4-carboxyaldehyde form of vitamin B6, it is converted into pyridoxal phosphate, a coenzyme for the synthesis of amino acids, neurotransmitters, sphingolipids and aminolevulinic acid.

name: penicillin
description: Any member of the group of substituted penams containing two methyl substituents at position 2, a carboxylate substituent at position 3 and a carboxamido group at position 6.

name: sulfite
description: A sulfur oxoanion that is the conjugate base of hydrogen sulfite (H2SO3).

name: (2S)-2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid
description: A 2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid in which the carbon at position 2 has (S)-configuration.

name: methylmalonate(2-)
description: A C4-dicarboxylate resulting from the removal of a proton from both carboxylic acid groups of methylmalonic acid.

name: aldehyde
description: A compound RC(=O)H, in which a carbonyl group is bonded to one hydrogen atom and to one R group.

name: homocystine
description: An organic disulfide obtained by oxidative dimerisation of homocysteine.

name: cyanide
description: A pseudohalide anion that is the conjugate base of hydrogen cyanide.

name: hydrogencarbonate
description: The carbon oxoanion resulting from the removal of a proton from carbonic acid.

name: toluene
description: The simplest member of the class toluenes consisting of a benzene core which bears a single methyl substituent.

name: 4-aminophenol
description: An amino phenol (one of the three possible isomers) which has the single amino substituent located para to the phenolic -OH group.

name: geroprotector
description: Any compound that supports healthy aging, slows the biological aging process, or extends lifespan.

name: vitamin B2
description: Any member of a group of vitamers that belong to the chemical structural class called flavins that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B2 deficiency. Symptoms associated with vitamin B2 deficiency include glossitis, seborrhea, angular stomaitis, cheilosis and photophobia. The vitamers include riboflavin and its phosphate derivatives (and includes their salt, ionised and hydrate forms).

name: vitamin B7
description: Any member of a group of vitamers that belong to the chemical structural class called biotins that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B7 deficiency. Vitamin B7 deficiency is very rare in individuals who take a normal balanced diet. Foods rich in biotin are egg yolk, liver, cereals, vegetables (spinach, mushrooms) and rice. Symptoms associated with vitamin B7 deficiency include thinning hair, scaly skin rashes around eyes, nose and mouth, and brittle nails. The vitamers include biotin and its ionized and salt forms.

name: vitamin B12
description: Any member of a group of cobalamin vitamers that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B12 deficiency. Vitamin B12 deficiency is associated with low red blood cell count and anemia. The vitamers are found in foods such as cereals, meat, fish, and poultry. The vitamers include adenosylcobalamin, hydroxocobalamin, cyanocobalamin, aquacobalamin, nitritocobalamin and methylcobabalamin (also includes their ionized, salt and phosphate derivatives).

name: ceramide
description: Ceramides (N-acyl-sphingoid bases) are a major subclass of sphingoid base derivatives with an amide-linked fatty acid. The fatty acids are typically saturated or monounsaturated with chain lengths from 14 to 26 carbon atoms; the presence of a hydroxyl group on carbon 2 is fairly common. Ceramides are generally precursors of more complex sphingolipids. In the illustrated generalised structure, R(1) = OH, OX (where X = acyl, glycosyl, phosphate, phosphonate, etc.), or H.

name: lumichrome
description: A compound showing blue fluorescence, formed by a photolysis of riboflavin in acid or neutral solution.

name: methanol
description: The primary alcohol that is the simplest aliphatic alcohol, comprising a methyl and an alcohol group.

name: organohalogen compound
description: A compound containing at least one carbon-halogen bond (where X is a halogen atom).

name: hydrogen chloride
description: A mononuclear parent hydride consisting of covalently bonded hydrogen and chlorine atoms.

name: donor
description: A molecular entity that can transfer ("donate") an electron, a pair of electrons, an atom or a group to another molecular entity.

name: (2R)-2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid
description: A 2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid having (2R)-configuration.

name: L-tyrosine
description: An optically active form of tyrosine having L-configuration.

name: chloride
description: A halide anion formed when chlorine picks up an electron to form an an anion.

name: dinitrogen
description: An elemental molecule consisting of two trivalently-bonded nitrogen atoms.

name: piperidine
description: An azacycloalkane that is cyclohexane in which one of the carbons is replaced by a nitrogen. It is a metabolite of cadaverine, a polyamine found in the human intestine.

name: lipid
description: 'Lipids' is a loosely defined term for substances of biological origin that are soluble in nonpolar solvents. They consist of saponifiable lipids, such as glycerides (fats and oils) and phospholipids, as well as nonsaponifiable lipids, principally steroids.

name: glycosaminoglycan
description: Any polysaccharide containing a substantial proportion of aminomonosaccharide residues.

name: hexose
description: Any six-carbon monosaccharide which in its linear form contains either an aldehyde group at position 1 (aldohexose) or a ketone group at position 2 (ketohexose).

name: polysaccharide
description: A biomacromolecule consisting of large numbers of monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically. This term is commonly used only for those containing more than ten monosaccharide residues.

name: tyrosine
description: An alpha-amino acid that is phenylalanine bearing a hydroxy substituent at position 4 on the phenyl ring.

name: glutamic acid
description: An alpha-amino acid that is glutaric acid bearing a single amino substituent at position 2.

name: iron atom
description: An iron group element atom that has atomic number 26.

name: alkane
description: An acyclic branched or unbranched hydrocarbon having the general formula CnH2n+2, and therefore consisting entirely of hydrogen atoms and saturated carbon atoms.

name: phosphate(3-)
description: A phosphate ion that is the conjugate base of hydrogenphosphate.

name: pyridoxal 5'-phosphate
description: The monophosphate ester obtained by condensation of phosphoric acid with the primary hydroxy group of pyridoxal.

name: hydrogen cyanide
description: A one-carbon compound consisting of a methine group triple bonded to a nitrogen atom

name: acetamides
description: Compounds with the general formula RNHC(=O)CH3.

name: acyl group
description: An organic group formed by removing one or more hydroxy groups from an oxoacid that has the general structure RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l =/= 0). Although the term is almost always applied to organic compounds, with carboxylic acid as the oxoacid, acyl groups can in principle be derived from other types of acids such as sulfonic acids or phosphonic acids.

name: aflatoxin
description: Any of a group of related and highly toxic secondary metabolites (mycotoxins) whose main structural feature is a fused coumarin-bis(dihydrofuran) ring system and which are produced by strains of the moulds Aspergillus flavus or A. parasiticus, together with further metabolites of these mycotoxins

name: alkaloid
description: Any of the naturally occurring, basic nitrogen compounds (mostly heterocyclic) occurring mostly in the plant kingdom, but also found in bacteria, fungi, and animals. By extension, certain neutral compounds biogenetically related to basic alkaloids are also classed as alkaloids. Amino acids, peptides, proteins, nucleotides, nucleic acids, amino sugars and antibiotics are not normally regarded as alkaloids. Compounds in which the nitrogen is  exocyclic (dopamine, mescaline, serotonin, etc.) are usually classed as amines rather than alkaloids.

name: alkyl group
description: A univalent group -CnH2n+1 derived from an alkane by removal of a hydrogen atom from any carbon atom.

name: alkylating agent
description: Highly reactive chemical that introduces alkyl radicals into biologically active molecules and thereby prevents their proper functioning. It could be used as an antineoplastic agent, but it might be very toxic, with carcinogenic, mutagenic, teratogenic, and immunosuppressant actions. It could also be used as a component of poison gases.

name: amino alcohol
description: An alcohol containing an amino functional group in addition to the alcohol-defining hydroxy group.

name: amino aldehyde
description: Any aldehyde which contains an amino group.

name: aminodiol
description: An amino alcohol having two hydroxy functional groups.

name: anilines
description: Any  aromatic amine that is benzene carrying at least one amino substituent and its substituted derivatives.

name: anion
description: A monoatomic or polyatomic species having one or more elementary charges of the electron.

name: antioxidant
description: A substance that opposes oxidation or inhibits reactions brought about by dioxygen or peroxides.

name: barbiturates
description: Members of the class of pyrimidones consisting of pyrimidine-2,4,6(1H,3H,5H)-trione (barbituric acid) and its derivatives. Largest group of the synthetic sedative/hypnotics, sharing a characteristic six-membered ring structure.

name: base
description: A molecular entity having an available pair of electrons capable of forming a covalent bond with a hydron (Bronsted base) or with the vacant orbital of some other molecular entity (Lewis base).

name: benzenes
description: Any benzenoid aromatic compound consisting of the benzene skeleton and its substituted derivatives.

name: benzoates
description: A monocarboxylic acid anion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group of any benzoic acid.

name: benzoic acids
description: Any aromatic carboxylic acid that consists of benzene in which at least a single hydrogen has been substituted by a carboxy group.

name: NMR chemical shift reference compound
description: Any compound that produces a peak used to reference an NMR spectrum during data pre-processing.

name: bile salt
description: A sodium salt of the conjugate of any bile acid with either glycine or taurine.

name: branched-chain amino acid
description: Any  amino acid  in which the parent hydrocarbon chain has one or more alkyl substituents

name: carbamoyl group
description: The univalent carboacyl group formed by loss of -OH from the carboxy group of carbamic acid.

name: EC 4.2.1.1 (carbonic anhydrase) inhibitor
description: An EC 4.2.1.* (hydro-lyases) inhibitor that interferes with the action of carbonic anhydrase (EC 4.2.1.1). Such compounds reduce the secretion of H(+) ions by the proximal kidney tubule.

name: cerebroside
description: Any member of a group of glycosphingolipids, also known as monoglycosylceramides, which are important components in animal muscle and nerve cell membranes.

name: chlorine molecular entity
description: A halogen molecular entity containing one or more atoms of chlorine.

name: chloroacetate
description: A haloacetate(1-) resulting from the deprotonation of the carboxy group of chloroacetic acid.

name: chlorobenzenes
description: Any organochlorine compound containing a benzene ring which is substituted by one or more chlorines.

name: cholines
description: A quaternary ammonium ion based on the choline ion and its substituted derivatives thereof.

name: coenzyme
description: A low-molecular-weight, non-protein organic compound participating in enzymatic reactions as dissociable acceptor or donor of chemical groups or electrons.

name: cofactor
description: An organic molecule or ion (usually a metal ion) that is required by an enzyme for its activity. It may be attached either loosely (coenzyme) or tightly (prosthetic group).

name: colchicine
description: An  alkaloid that is a carbotricyclic compound comprising 5,6,7,9-tetrahydrobenzo[a]heptalene having four methoxy substituents at the 1-, 2-, 3- and 10-positions as well as an oxo group at the 9-position and an acetamido group at the 7-position. It has been isolated from the plants belonging to genus Colchicum.

name: molecular entity
description: Any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, radical ion, complex, conformer etc., identifiable as a separately distinguishable entity.

name: cyclohexanones
description: Any alicyclic ketone based on a cyclohexane skeleton and its substituted derivatives thereof.

name: diol
description: A compound that contains two hydroxy groups, generally assumed to be, but not necessarily, alcoholic. Aliphatic diols are also called glycols.

name: diterpenoid
description: Any terpenoid derived from a diterpene. The term includes compounds in which the C20 skeleton of the parent diterpene has been rearranged or modified by the removal of one or more skeletal atoms (generally methyl groups).

name: drug
description: Any substance which when absorbed into a living organism may modify one or more of its functions. The term is generally accepted for a substance taken for a therapeutic purpose, but is also commonly used for abused substances.

name: enzyme inhibitor
description: A compound or agent that combines with an enzyme in such a manner as to prevent the normal substrate-enzyme combination and the catalytic reaction.

name: ethanediol
description: Any diol that is ethane or substituted ethane carrying two hydroxy groups.

name: fat-soluble vitamin (role)
description: Any vitamin that dissolves in fats and are stored in body tissues. Unlike the water-soluble vitamins, they are stored in the body for long periods of time and generally pose a greater risk for toxicity when consumed in excess.

name: furans
description: Compounds containing at least one furan ring.

name: glucocorticoid
description: Glucocorticoids are a class of steroid hormones that regulate a variety of physiological processes, in particular control of the concentration of glucose in blood.

name: glutamine family amino acid
description: An L-alpha-amino acid which is L-glutamic acid or any of the essential amino acids biosynthesised from it (glutamine, proline and arginine). A closed class.

name: EC 6.3.1.2 (glutamate--ammonia ligase) inhibitor
description: An EC 6.3.* (C-N bond-forming ligase) inhibitor that interferes with the action of glutamate--ammonia ligase (EC 6.3.1.2).

name: glycoside
description: A glycosyl compound resulting from the attachment of a glycosyl group to a non-acyl group RO-, RS-, RSe-, etc. The bond between the glycosyl group and the non-acyl group is called a glycosidic bond. By extension, the terms N-glycosides and C-glycosides are used as class names for glycosylamines and for compounds having a glycosyl group attached to a hydrocarbyl group respectively. These terms are misnomers and should not be used. The preferred terms are glycosylamines and C-glycosyl compounds, respectively.

name: glycosphingolipid
description: A glycosphingolipid is a glycolipid that is a carbohydrate-containing derivative of a sphingoid or ceramide. It is understood that the carbohydrate residue is attached by a glycosidic linkage to O-1 of the sphingoid.

name: chemical entity
description: A chemical entity is a physical entity of interest in chemistry including molecular entities, parts thereof, and chemical substances.

name: biological role
description: A role played by the molecular entity or part thereof within a biological context.

name: group
description: A defined linked collection of atoms or a single atom within a molecular entity.

name: herbicide
description: A substance used to destroy plant pests.

name: organic heterocyclic compound
description: A cyclic compound having as ring members atoms of carbon and at least of one other element.

name: heterodetic cyclic peptide
description: A heterodetic cyclic peptide is a peptide consisting only of amino-acid residues, but in which the linkages forming the ring are not solely peptide bonds; one or more is an isopeptide, disulfide, ester, or other bond.

name: homocystines
description: A non-proteinogenic alpha-amino acid obtained by oxidative dimerisation of homocysteine and its derivatives.

name: hormone
description: Originally referring to an endogenous compound that is formed in specialized organ or group of cells and carried to another organ or group of cells, in the same organism, upon which it has a specific regulatory function, the term is now commonly used to include non-endogenous, semi-synthetic and fully synthetic analogues of such compounds.

name: hydrocarbon
description: A compound consisting of carbon and hydrogen only.

name: hydroxides
description: Hydroxides are chemical compounds containing a hydroxy group or salts containing hydroxide (OH(-)).

name: hydroxy-amino acid
description: A non-proteinogenic alpha-amino acid bearing one or more hydroxy groups at unspecified positions.

name: hydroxy carboxylic acid
description: Any carboxylic acid with at least one hydroxy group.

name: hydroxybenzoate
description: Any benzoate derivative carrying a single carboxylate group and at least one hydroxy substituent.

name: hydroxybenzoic acid
description: Any benzoic acid carrying one or more phenolic hydroxy groups on the benzene ring.

name: hydroxypyridine
description: Any member of the class of pyridines with at least one hydroxy substituent.

name: oxoacid
description: A compound which contains oxygen, at least one other element, and at least one hydrogen bound to oxygen, and which produces a conjugate base by loss of positive hydrogen ion(s) (hydrons).

name: inorganic molecular entity
description: A molecular entity that contains no carbon.

name: salt
description: A salt is an assembly of cations and anions.

name: ion
description: A molecular entity having a net electric charge.

name: isoprenoid
description: Any lipid formally derived from isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene), the skeleton of which can generally be discerned in repeated occurrence in the molecule. The skeleton of isoprenoids may differ from strict additivity of isoprene units by loss or shift of a fragment, commonly a methyl group. The class includes both hydrocarbons and oxygenated derivatives.

name: lactam
description: Cyclic amides of amino carboxylic acids, having a 1-azacycloalkan-2-one structure, or analogues having unsaturation or heteroatoms replacing one or more carbon atoms of the ring.

name: lactate
description: A hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of lactic acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.

name: lactone
description: Any cyclic carboxylic ester containing a 1-oxacycloalkan-2-one structure, or an analogue having unsaturation or heteroatoms replacing one or more carbon atoms of the ring.

name: leucine
description: A branched-chain amino acid that consists of glycine in which one of the hydrogens attached to the alpha-carbon is substituted by an isobutyl group.

name: metabolite
description: Any intermediate or product resulting from metabolism. The term 'metabolite' subsumes the classes commonly known as primary and secondary metabolites.

name: methyl ester
description: Any carboxylic ester resulting from the formal condensation of a carboxy group with methanol.

name: methylpyridines
description: Any member of the class of pyridines that carries at least one methyl substituent.

name: mineralocorticoid
description: Mineralocorticoids are a class of steroid hormones that regulate water and electrolyte metabolism.

name: elemental molecule
description: A molecule all atoms of which have the same atomic number.

name: molecule
description: Any polyatomic entity that is an electrically neutral entity consisting of more than one atom.

name: monocarboxylic acid
description: An oxoacid containing a single carboxy group.

name: monohydroxybenzoate
description: A hydroxybenzoate carrying a single hydroxy substituent at unspecified position.

name: monohydroxybenzoic acid
description: Any hydroxybenzoic acid having a single phenolic hydroxy substituent on the benzene ring.

name: mutagen
description: An agent that increases the frequency of mutations above the normal background level, usually by interacting directly with DNA and causing it damage, including base substitution.

name: mycotoxin
description: Poisonous substance produced by fungi.

name: neurotransmitter
description: An endogenous compound that is used to transmit information across the synapse between a neuron and another cell.

name: neutral glycosphingolipid
description: Any glycosphingolipid containing unsubstituted glycosyl moieties.

name: organic anion
description: Any organic ion with a net negative charge.

name: organic cation
description: Any organic ion with a net positive charge.

name: ether
description: An organooxygen compound with formula ROR, where R is not hydrogen.

name: organic oxide
description: An oxide in which the oxygen atom is bonded to a carbon atom.

name: organic sulfate
description: Compounds of the general formula SO3HOR where R is an organyl group

name: aliphatic alcohol
description: An  alcohol derived from an aliphatic compound.

name: organophosphorus compound
description: An organophosphorus compound is formally a compound containing at least one carbon-phosphorus bond, but the term is often extended to include esters and thioesters.

name: oxide
description: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with other chemical elements.

name: peptide hormone
description: Any peptide with hormonal activity in animals, whether endocrine, neuroendocrine, or paracrine.

name: pesticide
description: Strictly, a substance intended to kill pests. In common usage, any substance used for controlling, preventing, or destroying animal, microbiological or plant pests.

name: phenylalanine derivative
description: An amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of alanine at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of phenylalanine  by a heteroatom. The definition normally excludes peptides containing phenylalanine  residues.

name: phosphate
description: Salts and esters of phosphoric and oligophosphoric acids and their chalcogen analogues. In inorganic chemistry, the term is also used to describe anionic coordination entities with phosphorus as central atom.

name: phosphoric acid
description: A phosphorus oxoacid that consists of one oxo and three hydroxy groups joined covalently to a central phosphorus atom.

name: plant growth regulator
description: A chemical, natural or artificial, that can affect the rate of growth of a plant.

name: polar amino acid
description: Any amino acid whose side chain is capable of forming one or more hydrogen bonds.

name: polyketide
description: Natural and synthetic compounds containing alternating carbonyl and methylene groups ('beta-polyketones'), biogenetically derived from repeated condensation of acetyl coenzyme A (via malonyl coenzyme A), and usually the compounds derived from them by further condensations, etc. Considered by many to be synonymous with the less frequently used terms acetogenins and ketides.

name: polyol
description: A compound that contains two or more hydroxy groups.

name: porphyrins
description: Natural pigments containing a fundamental skeleton of four pyrrole nuclei united through the alpha-positions by four methine groups to form a macrocyclic structure.

name: prosthetic group
description: A tightly bound, specific nonpolypeptide unit in a protein determining and involved in its biological activity.

name: purines
description: A class of imidazopyrimidines that consists of purine and its substituted derivatives.

name: pyridines
description: Any organonitrogen heterocyclic compound based on a pyridine skeleton and its substituted derivatives.

name: quaternary nitrogen compound
description: A nitrogen molecular entity that is electronically neutral but which contains a quaternary nitrogen.

name: retinoic acid
description: A retinoid consisting of 3,7-dimethylnona-2,4,6,8-tetraenoic acid substituted at position 9 by a 2,6,6-trimethylcyclohex-1-en-1-yl group (geometry of the four exocyclic double bonds is not specified).

name: retinoid
description: Oxygenated derivatives of 3,7-dimethyl-1-(2,6,6-trimethylcyclohex-1-enyl)nona-1,3,5,7-tetraene and derivatives thereof.

name: salicylates
description: Any salt or ester arising from reaction of the carboxy group of salicylic acid, or any ester resulting from the condensation of the phenolic hydroxy group of salicylic acid with an organic acid.

name: saponin
description: A glycoside that is a compound containing one or more hydrophilic glycoside moieties combined with a lipophilic triterpenoid or steroid derivative. Found in particular abundance in plant species.

name: sapogenin
description: Any organic polycyclic compound that is the aglycon moiety of a saponin; sapogenins may be steroids or triterpenoids.

name: saturated fatty acid
description: Any fatty acid containing no carbon to carbon multiple bonds. Known to produce adverse biological effects when ingested to excess.

name: short-chain fatty acid
description: An aliphatic monocarboxylic acid with a chain length of less than C6. If any non-hydrocarbon substituent is present, the compound is not normally regarded as a short-chain fatty acid.

name: sodium chloride
description: An inorganic chloride salt having sodium(1+) as the counterion.

name: sodium salt
description: Any alkali metal salt having sodium(1+) as the cation.

name: sphingenine
description: A 2-aminooctadecene-1,3-diol having (2S,3R)-configuration.

name: sphingolipid
description: Sphingolipids are a complex family of compounds that share a common structural feature, a sphingoid base backbone.

name: sphing-4-enine
description: A sphingenine in which the C=C double bond is located at the 4-position.

name: steroid hormone
description: Any steroid that acts as hormone.

name: amphetamine
description: A racemate comprising equimolar amounts of (R)-amphetamine (also known as levamphetamine or levoamphetamine) and (S)-amphetamine (also known as dexamfetamine or dextroamphetamine.

name: sulfuric ester
description: An ester of an alcohol and sulfuric acid.

name: sulfates
description: Salts and esters of sulfuric acid

name: sulfuric acid
description: A sulfur oxoacid that consists of two oxo and two hydroxy groups joined covalently to a central sulfur atom.

name: terpenoid
description: Any isoprenoid that is a natural product or related compound formally derived from isoprene units. Terpenoids may contain oxygen in various functional groups. This class is subdivided according to the number of carbon atoms in the parent terpene. The skeleton of terpenoids may differ from strict additivity of isoprene units by the loss or shift of a fragment, generally a methyl group.

name: tertiary alcohol
description: A tertiary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, -OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has three other carbon atoms attached to it.

name: tetracyclines
description: A subclass of polyketides having an octahydrotetracene-2-carboxamide skeleton, substituted with many hydroxy and other groups.

name: tetrapyrrole
description: A natural pigment containing four pyrrole rings joined by one-carbon units linking position 2 of one pyrrole ring to position 5 of the next.

name: vitamin B1
description: Any member of the group of 1,3-thiazolium cations that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B1 deficiency in animals. Symptoms of vitamin B1 deficiency include constipation, loss of apetite, fatigue, nausea, delirium, blurry vision and muscle weakness. Severe vitamin B1 deficiency can also lead to a disease known as beriberi. Vitamin B1 consists of the vitamer thiamin and its acid, aldehyde and phosphorylated derivatives (and their corresponding ionized, salt and hydrate forms).

name: organic heterotricyclic compound
description: An organic tricyclic compound in which at least one of the rings of the tricyclic skeleton contains one or more heteroatoms.

name: toluenes
description: Any member of the class of benzenes that is a substituted benzene in which the substituents include one (and only one) methyl group.

name: toxin
description: Poisonous substance produced by a biological organism such as a microbe, animal or plant.

name: micronutrient
description: Any nutrient required in small quantities by organisms throughout their life in order to orchestrate a range of physiological functions.

name: transition element atom
description: An element whose atom has an incomplete d sub-shell, or which can give rise to cations with an incomplete d sub-shell.

name: L-tyrosine derivative
description: A proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of L-tyrosine at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of L-tyrosine by a heteroatom.

name: univalent carboacyl group
description: A univalent carboacyl group is a group formed by loss of OH from the carboxy group of a carboxylic acid.

name: uric acid
description: An oxopurine that is the final oxidation product of purine metabolism.

name: valine
description: A branched-chain amino acid that consists of glycine in which one of the hydrogens attached to the alpha-carbon is substituted by an isopropyl group.

name: vitamin D
description: Any member of a group of fat-soluble hydroxy seco-steroids that exhibit biological activity against vitamin D deficiency. Vitamin D  can be obtained from sun exposure, food and supplements and is biologically inactive and converted into the biologically active calcitriol via double hydroxylation in the body.

name: vitamin B6
description: Any member of the group of pyridines that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B6 deficiency. Vitamin B6 deficiency is associated with microcytic anemia, electroencephalographic abnormalities, dermatitis with cheilosis (scaling on the lips and cracks at the corners of the mouth) and glossitis (swollen tongue), depression and confusion, and weakened immune function. Vitamin B6 consists of the vitamers pyridoxine, pyridoxal, and pyridoxamine and their respective 5'-phosphate esters (and includes their corresponding ionized and salt forms).

name: water-soluble vitamin (role)
description: Any vitamin that dissolves in water and readily absorbed into tissues for immediate use. Unlike the fat-soluble vitamins, they are not stored in the body and need to be replenished regularly in the diet and will rarely accumulate to toxic levels since they are quickly excreted from the body via urine.

name: zwitterion
description: A neutral compound having formal unit electrical charges of opposite sign on non-adjacent atoms. Sometimes referred to as inner salts, dipolar ions (a misnomer).

name: aldosterone
description: A pregnane-based steroidal hormone produced by the outer-section (zona glomerulosa) of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland, and acts on the distal tubules and collecting ducts of the kidney to cause the conservation of sodium, secretion of potassium, increased water retention, and increased blood pressure. The overall effect of aldosterone is to increase reabsorption of ions and water in the kidney.

name: cobalt atom
description: A cobalt group element atom that has atomic number 27.

name: chloroacetic acid
description: A chlorocarboxylic acid that is acetic acid carrying a 2-chloro substituent.

name: tetracycline
description: A broad-spectrum polyketide antibiotic produced by the Streptomyces genus of actinobacteria.

name: beta-lactam antibiotic
description: An organonitrogen heterocyclic antibiotic that contains a beta-lactam ring.

name: cocaine
description: A tropane alkaloid obtained from leaves of the South American shrub Erythroxylon coca.

name: phenylalanine
description: An aromatic amino acid that is alanine in which one of the methyl hydrogens is substituted by a phenyl group.

name: nickel atom
description: Chemical element (nickel group element atom) with atomic number 28.

name: rac-lactic acid
description: A racemate comprising equimolar amounts of (R)- and (S)-lactic acid.

name: D-tyrosine
description: An optically active form of tyrosine having D-configuration.

name: carbamic acid
description: A one-carbon compound that is ammonia in which one of the hydrogens is replaced by a carboxy group. Although carbamic acid derivatives are common, carbamic acid itself has never been synthesised.

name: aminophenol
description: A substituted aniline carrying a hydroxy substituent. A 'closed class'.

name: fatty acid anion
description: The conjugate base of a fatty acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxylic acid group of the corresponding fatty acid.

name: ammonium
description: An onium cation obtained by protonation of ammonia.

name: dicarboxylic acid dianion
description: A carboxylic acid dianion obtained by deprotonation of both carboxy groups of any dicarboxylic acid.

name: carboxylic acid anion
description: The conjugate base formed when the carboxy group of a carboxylic acid is deprotonated.

name: sodium(1+)
description: A monoatomic monocation obtained from sodium.

name: potassium(1+)
description: A monoatomic monocation obtained from potassium.

name: isocyanic acid
description: A colourless, volatile, poisonous inorganic compound with the formula HNCO; the simplest stable chemical compound that contains carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, and oxygen, the four most commonly-found elements in organic chemistry and biology.

name: hydridonitrate(2-)
description: A divalent inorganic anion resulting from the removal of two protons from ammonia.

name: monocarboxylic acid amide
description: A carboxamide derived from a monocarboxylic acid.

name: barbiturate
description: Conjugate base of barbituric acid.

name: L-glutamate(1-)
description: An alpha-amino-acid anion that is the conjugate base of L-glutamic acid, having anionic carboxy groups and a cationic amino group

name: D-glutamate(1-)
description: An alpha-amino-acid anion that is the conjugate base of D-glutamic acid, having anionic carboxy groups and a cationic amino group

name: glutamate(2-)
description: A dicarboxylic acid dianion that is the conjugate base of glutamate(1-).

name: L-glutamate(2-)
description: An L-alpha-amino acid anion that is the dianion obtained by the deprotonation of the both the carboxy groups of L-glutamic acid.

name: acetate
description: A monocarboxylic acid anion resulting from the removal of a proton from the carboxy group of acetic acid.

name: isobutane
description: An alkane that is propane substituted by a methyl group at position 2.

name: cobalamin
description: A cobalt-corrinoid hexaamide that is cobalamin with the oxidation state of the central cobalt atom unspecified.

name: heme
description: A heme is any tetrapyrrolic chelate of iron.

name: beryllium atom
description: Alkaline earth metal atom with atomic number 4.

name: flavin
description: A derivative of the dimethylisoalloxazine (7,8-dimethylbenzo[g]pteridine-2,4(3H,10H)-dione) skeleton, with a substituent on the 10 position.

name: silicon dioxide
description: A silicon oxide made up of linear triatomic molecules in which a silicon atom is covalently bonded to two oxygens.

name: ethylene glycol
description: A 1,2-glycol compound produced via reaction of ethylene oxide with water.

name: benzoic acid
description: A compound comprising a benzene ring core carrying a carboxylic acid substituent.

name: formic acid
description: The simplest carboxylic acid, containing a single carbon. Occurs naturally in various sources including the venom of bee and ant stings, and is a useful organic synthetic reagent. Principally used as a preservative and antibacterial agent in livestock feed. Induces severe metabolic acidosis and ocular injury in human subjects.

name: salicylate
description: A monohydroxybenzoate that is the conjugate base of salicylic acid.

name: propionic acid
description: A short-chain saturated fatty acid comprising ethane attached to the carbon of a carboxy group.

name: malonic acid
description: An alpha,omega-dicarboxylic acid in which the two carboxy groups are separated by a single methylene group.

name: methylmalonic acid
description: A dicarboxylic acid that is malonic acid in which one of the methylene hydrogens is substituted by a methyl group.

name: methylmalonate(1-)
description: A dicarboxylic acid monoanion resulting from the removal of a proton from one of the carboxylic acid groups of methylmalonic acid.

name: alcohol
description: A compound in which a hydroxy group, -OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom.

name: 4,4'-bipyridine
description: A  bipyridine in which the two pyridine moieties are linked by a bond between positions C-4 and C-4'.

name: L-phenylalaninate
description: An optically active form of phenylalaninate having L-configuration.

name: L-phenylalaninium
description: An optically active form of phenylalaninium having L-configuration.

name: D-phenylalaninate
description: The D-enantiomer of phenylalaninate.

name: D-phenylalaninium
description: An optically active form of phenylalaninium having D-configuration.

name: phenylalaninate
description: An aromatic amino-acid anion that is the conjugate base of phenylalanine, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.

name: phenylalaninium
description: An alpha-amino-acid cation that is the conjugate acid of phenylalanine, arising from protonation of the amino group.

name: tetracene
description: An acene that consists of four ortho-fused benzene rings in a rectilinear arrangement.

name: leucinate
description: An alpha-amino-acid anion that is the conjugate base of leucine, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.

name: leucinium
description: An alpha-amino-acid cation that is the conjugate acid of leucine, arising from protonation of the amino group.

name: L-tyrosinate(1-)
description: An optically active form of tyrosinate having L-configuration.

name: L-tyrosinate(2-)
description: The L-enantiomer of tyrosinate(2-).

name: L-tyrosinium
description: An optically active form of tyrosinium having L-configuration.

name: D-tyrosinate(1-)
description: An optically active form of tyrosinate(1-) having D-configuration.

name: D-tyrosinate(2-)
description: The D-enantiomer of tyrosinate(2-).

name: D-tyrosinium
description: An optically active form of tyrosinium having D-configuration.

name: tyrosinate(1-)
description: An alpha-amino-acid anion that is the conjugate base of tyrosine, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.

name: tyrosinium
description: An alpha-amino-acid cation that is the conjugate acid of tyrosine, arising from protonation of the amino group.

name: secondary amine
description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing two hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

name: tertiary amine
description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

name: primary amine
description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one hydrogen atom by a hydrocarbyl group.

name: amine
description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

name: amide
description: An amide is a derivative of an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l =/= 0) in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.

name: vitamin (role)
description: A biochemical role played by any micronutrient that is an organic compound. Vitamins are present in foods in small amounts and are essential to normal metabolism and biochemical functions, usually as coenzymes. The term "vitamines" (from vita + amines) was coined in 1912 by Casimir Funk, who believed that these compounds were amines.

name: application
description: Intended use of the molecular entity or part thereof by humans.

name: fundamental particle
description: A particle not known to have substructure.

name: monoatomic entity
description: A monoatomic entity is a molecular entity consisting of a single atom.

name: coordination entity
description: An assembly consisting of a central atom (usually metallic) to which is attached a surrounding array of other groups of atoms (ligands).

name: organic fundamental parent
description: An organic fundamental parent is a structure used as a basis for substitutive names in organic nomenclature, containing, in addition to one or more hydrogen atoms, a single atom of an element, a number of atoms (alike or different) linked together to form an unbranched chain, a monocyclic or polycyclic ring system, or a ring assembly or ring/chain system.

name: inorganic group
description: Any substituent group which does not contain carbon.

name: organic group
description: Any substituent group or skeleton containing carbon.

name: hydrocarbyl group
description: A univalent group formed by removing a hydrogen atom from a hydrocarbon.

name: organyl group
description: Any organic substituent group, regardless of functional type, having one free valence at a carbon atom.

name: atom
description: A chemical entity constituting the smallest component of an element having the chemical properties of the element.

name: atomic nucleus
description: A nucleus is the positively charged central portion of an atom, excluding the orbital electrons.

name: nucleon
description: Heavy nuclear particle: proton or neutron.

name: primary amide
description: A derivative of an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l =/= 0) in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.

name: elemental molecular entity
description: A molecular entity all atoms of which have the same atomic number.

name: organosulfur compound
description: An organosulfur compound is a compound containing at least one carbon-sulfur bond.

name: polyatomic anion
description: An anion consisting of more than one atom.

name: antimicrobial agent
description: A substance that kills or slows the growth of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoans.

name: antibacterial agent
description: A substance (or active part thereof) that kills or slows the growth of bacteria.

name: nutrient
description: A nutrient is a food component that an organism uses to survive and grow.

name: heteroorganic entity
description: A heteroorganic entity is an organic molecular entity in which carbon atoms or organic groups are bonded directly to one or more heteroatoms.

name: agrochemical
description: An agrochemical is a substance that is used in agriculture or horticulture.

name: fertilizer
description: A fertilizer is any substance that is added to soil or water to assist the growth of plants.

name: food
description: A physiological role played by any substance of either plant, animal or artificial origin which contains essential body nutrients that can be ingested by an organism to provide energy, promote growth, and maintain the processes of life.

name: fuel
description: An energy-rich substance that can be transformed with release of usable energy.

name: diagnostic agent
description: A substance administered to aid diagnosis of a disease.

name: alkali metal molecular entity
description: A molecular entity containing one or more atoms of an alkali metal.

name: alkaline earth molecular entity
description: An alkaline earth molecular entity is a molecular entity containing one or more atoms of an alkaline earth metal.

name: pnictogen
description: Any p-block element atom that is in group 15 of the periodic table: nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, antimony and bismuth.

name: pnictogen molecular entity
description: A p-block molecular entity containing any pnictogen.

name: chalcogen
description: Any p-block element belonging to the group 16 family of the periodic table.

name: chalcogen molecular entity
description: Any p-block molecular entity containing a chalcogen.

name: carboxylic ester
description: An ester of a carboxylic acid, R(1)C(=O)OR(2), where R(1) = H or organyl and R(2) = organyl.

name: main group element atom
description: An atom belonging to one of the main groups (found in the s- and p- blocks) of the periodic table.

name: hydracid
description: A hydracid is a compound which contains hydrogen that is not bound to oxygen, and which produces a conjugate base by loss of positive hydrogen ion(s) (hydrons).

name: benzylic group
description: Arylmethyl groups and derivatives formed by substitution: ArCR2-.

name: phosphorus oxoacid
description: A pnictogen oxoacid which contains phosphorus and oxygen, at least one hydrogen atom bound to oxygen, and forms an ion by the loss of one or more protons.

name: transition element molecular entity
description: A molecular entity containing one or more atoms of a transition element.

name: metal atom
description: An atom of an element that exhibits typical metallic properties, being typically shiny, with high electrical and thermal conductivity.

name: sulfonate
description: The sulfur oxoanion formed by deprotonation of sulfonic acid.

name: alpha-amino-acid anion
description: An amino-acid anion obtained by deprotonation of any alpha-amino acid.

name: p-block element atom
description: Any main group element atom belonging to the p-block of the periodic table.

name: glycolipid
description: Any member of class of 1,2-di-O-acylglycerols joined at oxygen 3 by a glycosidic linkage to a carbohydrate part (usually a mono-, di- or tri-saccharide). Some substances classified as bacterial glycolipids have the sugar part acylated by one or more fatty acids and the glycerol part may be absent.

name: carboxylic acid
description: A carbon oxoacid acid carrying at least one -C(=O)OH group and having the structure RC(=O)OH, where R is any any monovalent functional group. Carboxylic acids are the most common type of organic acid.

name: sulfur-containing carboxylic acid
description: Any carboxylic acid having a sulfur substituent.

name: main group molecular entity
description: A molecular entity containing one or more atoms from any of groups 1, 2, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18 of the periodic table.

name: noble gas molecular entity
description: A main group molecular entity containing one or more atoms of any noble gas.

name: cyclic compound
description: Any molecule that consists of a series of atoms joined together to form a ring.

name: homocyclic compound
description: A cyclic compound having as ring members atoms of the same element only.

name: carbocyclic compound
description: A homocyclic compound in which all of the ring members are carbon atoms.

name: bicyclic compound
description: A molecule that features two fused rings.

name: ortho-fused compound
description: A polycyclic compound in which two rings have two, and only two, atoms in common. Such compounds have n common faces and 2n common atoms.

name: aliphatic compound
description: Any acyclic or cyclic, saturated or unsaturated carbon compound, excluding aromatic compounds.

name: alicyclic compound
description: An aliphatic compound having a carbocyclic ring structure which may be saturated or unsaturated, but may not be a benzenoid or other aromatic system.

name: aromatic compound
description: A cyclically conjugated molecular entity with a stability (due to delocalization) significantly greater than that of a hypothetical localized structure (e.g. Kekule structure) is said to possess aromatic character.

name: arene
description: Any monocyclic or polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon.

name: annulene
description: A mancude monocyclic hydrocarbon without side chains of the general formula CnHn (n is an even number) or CnHn+1 (n is an odd number). In systematic nomenclature an annulene with seven or more carbon atoms may be named [n]annulene, where n is the number of carbon atoms.

name: heteropolycyclic compound
description: A polycyclic compound in which at least one of the rings contains at least one non-carbon atom.

name: heterobicyclic compound
description: A bicyclic compound in which at least one of the rings contains at least one skeletal heteroatom.

name: s-block molecular entity
description: An s-block molecular entity is a molecular entity containing one or more atoms of an s-block element.

name: p-block molecular entity
description: A main group molecular entity that contains one or more atoms of a p-block element.

name: d-block molecular entity
description: A d-block molecular entity is a molecular entity containing one or more atoms of a d-block element.

name: hydrides
description: Hydrides are chemical compounds of hydrogen with other chemical elements.

name: biomacromolecule
description: A macromolecule formed by a living organism.

name: polyatomic cation
description: A cation consisting of more than one atom.

name: alpha-amino acid
description: An amino acid in which the amino group is located on the carbon atom at the position alpha to the carboxy group.

name: amino-acid residue
description: When two or more amino acids combine to form a peptide, the elements of water are removed, and what remains of each amino acid is called an amino-acid residue.

name: amino acid
description: A carboxylic acid containing one or more amino groups.

name: alpha-amino-acid residue
description: An amino-acid residue derived from an alpha-amino acid.

name: organic hydroxy compound
description: An organic compound having at least one hydroxy group attached to a carbon atom.

name: organic cyclic compound
description: Any organic molecule that consists of atoms connected in the form of a ring.

name: heteroarene
description: A heterocyclic compound formally derived from an arene by replacement of one or more methine (-C=) and/or vinylene (-CH=CH-) groups by trivalent or divalent heteroatoms, respectively, in such a way as to maintain the continuous pi-electron system characteristic of aromatic systems and a number of out-of-plane pi-electrons corresponding to the Hueckel rule (4n+2).

name: conjugated protein
description: Conjugated protein is a protein that contains a non-peptide component, usually in stoichiometric proportion.

name: macromolecule
description: A macromolecule is a molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

name: monocyclic arene
description: A monocyclic aromatic hydrocarbon.

name: polycyclic arene
description: A polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon.

name: phenols
description: Organic aromatic compounds having one or more hydroxy groups attached to a benzene or other arene ring.

name: aromatic amino acid
description: An amino acid whose structure includes an aromatic ring.

name: aromatic carboxylic acid
description: Any carboxylic acid in which the carboxy group is directly bonded to an aromatic ring.

name: aromatic amine
description: An amino compound in which the amino group is linked directly to an aromatic system.

name: reagent
description: A substance used in a chemical reaction to detect, measure, examine, or produce other substances.

name: corrinoid
description: A derivative of the corrin nucleus, which contains four reduced or partly reduced pyrrole rings joined in a macrocycle by three =C- groups and one direct carbon-carbon bond linking alpha positions.

name: aldohexose
description: A hexose with a (potential) aldehyde group at one end.

name: macronutrient
description: Any nutrient required in large quantities by organisms throughout their life in order to orchestrate a range of physiological functions. Macronutrients are usually chemical elements (carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur) that humans consume in the largest quantities. Calcium, sodium, magnesium and potassium are sometimes included as macronutrients because they are required in relatively large quantities compared with other vitamins and minerals.

name: paraquat
description: An organic cation that consists of 4,4'-bipyridine bearing two N-methyl substituents loctated at the 1- and 1'-positions.

name: azane
description: Saturated acyclic nitrogen hydrides having the general formula NnHn+2.

name: hemoprotein
description: Conjugated proteins containing heme as the prosthetic group.

name: terpene
description: A hydrocarbon of biological origin having carbon skeleton formally derived from isoprene [CH2=C(CH3)CH=CH2].

name: diterpene
description: A C20 terpene.

name: triterpene
description: A C30 terpene.

name: antimetabolite
description: A substance which is structurally similar to a metabolite but which competes with it or replaces it, and so prevents or reduces its normal utilization.

name: inhibitor
description: A substance that diminishes the rate of a chemical reaction.

name: catalyst
description: A substance that increases the rate of a reaction without modifying the overall standard Gibbs energy change in the reaction.

name: fossil fuel
description: A fuel such as coal, oil and natural gas which has formed over many years through the decomposition of deposited vegetation which was under extreme pressure of an overburden of earth.

name: amino acid zwitterion
description: The zwitterionic form of an amino acid having a negatively charged carboxyl group and a positively charged amino group.

name: quaternary ammonium ion
description: A derivative of ammonium, NH4(+), in which all four of the hydrogens bonded to nitrogen have been replaced with univalent (usually organyl) groups.

name: ammonium ion derivative
description: A derivative of ammonium, NH4(+), in which one (or more) of the hydrogens bonded to the nitrogen have been replaced with univalent organyl groups. The substituting carbon of the organyl group must not itself be directly attached to a heteroatom (thereby excluding protonated amides, hemiaminals, etc).

name: onium betaine
description: Neutral molecules having charge-separated forms with an onium atom which bears no hydrogen atoms and that is not adjacent to the anionic atom.

name: ammonium betaine
description: Any neutral molecule having charge-separated forms with a quaternary ammonium atom which bears no hydrogen atoms and that is not adjacent to the anionic atom.

name: fused compound
description: A polycyclic compound that contains more than one ring with at least two common atoms (also known as bridgehead carbons) that are adjacent to each other.

name: carbopolycyclic compound
description: A polyclic compound in which all of the ring members are carbon atoms.

name: acene
description: A polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon consisting of fused benzene rings in a rectilinear arrangement.

name: central nervous system stimulant
description: Any drug that enhances the activity of the central nervous system.

name: amphetamines
description: Amines that constitute a class of central nervous system stimulants based on the structure of the parent amphetamine 1-phenylpropan-2-amine.

name: steroid
description: Any of naturally occurring compounds and synthetic analogues, based on the cyclopenta[a]phenanthrene carbon skeleton, partially or completely hydrogenated; there are usually methyl groups at C-10 and C-13, and often an alkyl group at C-17. By extension, one or more bond scissions, ring expansions and/or ring contractions of the skeleton may have occurred. Natural steroids are derived biogenetically from squalene which is a triterpene.

name: 11beta-hydroxy steroid
description: Any 11-hydroxy steroid in which the hydroxy group at position 11 has beta- configuration.

name: 3beta-sterol
description: A sterol in which the hydroxy group at position 3 has beta- configuration.

name: organonitrogen compound
description: Any heteroorganic entity containing at least one carbon-nitrogen bond.

name: sulfonamide
description: An amide of a sulfonic acid RS(=O)2NR'2.

name: fatty acid
description: Any aliphatic monocarboxylic acid derived from or contained in esterified form in an animal or vegetable fat, oil or wax. Natural fatty acids commonly have a chain of 4 to 28 carbons (usually unbranched and even-numbered), which may be saturated or unsaturated. By extension, the term is sometimes used to embrace all acyclic aliphatic carboxylic acids.

name: monosaccharide
description: Parent monosaccharides are polyhydroxy aldehydes H[CH(OH)]nC(=O)H or polyhydroxy ketones H-[CHOH]n-C(=O)[CHOH]m-H with three or more carbon atoms. The generic term 'monosaccharide' (as opposed to oligosaccharide or polysaccharide) denotes a single unit, without glycosidic connection to other such units. It includes aldoses, dialdoses, aldoketoses, ketoses and diketoses, as well as deoxy sugars, provided that the parent compound has a (potential) carbonyl group.

name: oxoanion
description: An oxoanion is an anion derived from an oxoacid by loss of hydron(s) bound to oxygen.

name: antiinfective agent
description: A substance used in the prophylaxis or therapy of infectious diseases.

name: antiparasitic agent
description: A substance used to treat or prevent parasitic infections.

name: antidepressant
description: Antidepressants are mood-stimulating drugs used primarily in the treatment of affective disorders and related conditions.

name: central nervous system drug
description: A class of drugs producing both physiological and psychological effects through a variety of mechanisms involving the central nervous system.

name: psychotropic drug
description: A loosely defined grouping of drugs that have effects on psychological function.

name: anti-inflammatory drug
description: A substance that reduces or suppresses inflammation.

name: non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug
description: An anti-inflammatory drug that is not a steroid. In addition to anti-inflammatory actions, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs have analgesic, antipyretic, and platelet-inhibitory actions. They act by blocking the synthesis of prostaglandins by inhibiting cyclooxygenase, which converts arachidonic acid to cyclic endoperoxides, precursors of prostaglandins.

name: analgesic
description: An agent capable of relieving pain without the loss of consciousness or without producing anaesthesia. In addition, analgesic is a role played by a compound which is exhibited by a capability to cause a reduction of pain symptoms.

name: non-narcotic analgesic
description: A drug that has principally analgesic, antipyretic and anti-inflammatory actions. Non-narcotic analgesics do not bind to opioid receptors.

name: central nervous system depressant
description: A loosely defined group of drugs that tend to reduce the activity of the central nervous system.

name: organic disulfide
description: Compounds of structure RSSR in which R and R' are organic groups.

name: antipyretic
description: A drug that prevents or reduces fever by lowering the body temperature from a raised state. An antipyretic will not affect the normal body temperature if one does not have fever. Antipyretics cause the hypothalamus to override an interleukin-induced increase in temperature. The body will then work to lower the temperature and the result is a reduction in fever.

name: diuretic
description: An agent that promotes the excretion of urine through its effects on kidney function.

name: bronchodilator agent
description: An agent that causes an increase in the expansion of a bronchus or bronchial tubes.

name: sympathomimetic agent
description: A drug that mimics the effects of stimulating postganglionic adrenergic sympathetic nerves. Included in this class are drugs that directly stimulate adrenergic receptors and drugs that act indirectly by provoking the release of adrenergic transmitters.

name: hypoglycemic agent
description: A drug which lowers the blood glucose level.

name: EC 1.14.99.1 (prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase) inhibitor
description: A compound or agent that combines with cyclooxygenases (EC 1.14.99.1) and thereby prevents its substrate-enzyme combination with arachidonic acid and the formation of icosanoids, prostaglandins, and thromboxanes.

name: cardiovascular drug
description: A drug that affects the rate or intensity of cardiac contraction, blood vessel diameter or blood volume.

name: mancude ring
description: Any molecular entity that consists of a ring having (formally) the maximum number of noncumulative double bonds.

name: carbon oxoanion
description: A negative ion consisting solely of carbon and oxygen  atoms, and therefore having the general formula CxOy(n-) for some integers x, y and n.

name: antineoplastic agent
description: A substance that inhibits or prevents the proliferation of neoplasms.

name: aromatic ether
description: Any ether in which the oxygen is attached to at least one aryl substituent.

name: vasodilator agent
description: A drug used to cause dilation of the blood vessels.

name: anticonvulsant
description: A drug used to prevent seizures or reduce their severity.

name: beta-lactam
description: A lactam in which the amide bond is contained within a four-membered ring, which includes the amide nitrogen and the carbonyl carbon.

name: adrenergic uptake inhibitor
description: Adrenergic uptake inhibitors are drugs that block the transport of adrenergic transmitters into axon terminals or into storage vesicles within terminals. The tricyclic antidepressants and amphetamines are among the therapeutically important drugs that may act via inhibition of adrenergic transport. Many of these drugs also block transport of serotonin.

name: secondary alcohol
description: A secondary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, -OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has two other carbon atoms attached to it.

name: dicarboxylic acid
description: Any carboxylic acid containing two carboxy groups.

name: dicarboxylic acid monoanion
