description: Any dicarboxylic acid anion that is a monoanion obtained by the deprotonation of only one of the carboxy groups of the dicarboxylic acid.

name: ester
description: A compound formally derived from an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l > 0) and an alcohol, phenol, heteroarenol, or enol by linking with formal loss of water from an acidic hydroxy group of the former and a hydroxy group of the latter.

name: xenobiotic
description: A xenobiotic (Greek, xenos "foreign"; bios "life") is a compound that is foreign to a living organism. Principal xenobiotics include: drugs, carcinogens and various compounds that have been introduced into the environment by artificial means.

name: immunosuppressive agent
description: An agent that suppresses immune function by one of several mechanisms of action. Classical cytotoxic immunosuppressants act by inhibiting DNA synthesis. Others may act through activation of T-cells or by inhibiting the activation of helper cells. In addition, an immunosuppressive agent is a role played by a compound which is exhibited by a capability to diminish the extent and/or voracity of an immune response.

name: antifungal agent
description: An  antimicrobial agent that destroys fungi by suppressing their ability to grow or reproduce.

name: monocarboxylic acid anion
description: A carboxylic acid anion formed when the carboxy group of a monocarboxylic acid is deprotonated.

name: phosphate ion
description: A phosphorus oxoanion that is the conjugate base of phosphoric acid.

name: sphingoid
description: Sphinganine, its homologs and stereoisomers, and the hydroxy and unsaturated derivatives of these compounds.

name: antiprotozoal drug
description: Any antimicrobial drug which is used to treat or prevent protozoal infections.

name: antirheumatic drug
description: A drug used to treat rheumatoid arthritis.

name: lipoxygenase inhibitor
description: A compound or agent that combines with lipoxygenase and thereby prevents its substrate-enzyme combination with arachidonic acid and the formation of the icosanoid products hydroxyicosatetraenoic acid and various leukotrienes.

name: hydroxy monocarboxylic acid
description: Any monocarboxylic acid which also contains a separate (alcoholic or phenolic) hydroxy substituent.

name: neurotransmitter agent
description: A substance used for its pharmacological action on any aspect of neurotransmitter systems. Neurotransmitter agents include agonists, antagonists, degradation inhibitors, uptake inhibitors, depleters, precursors, and modulators of receptor function.

name: penams
description: Natural and synthetic antibiotics containing the 4-thia-1-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptan-7-one structure, generally assumed to have the 5R configuration unless otherwise specified.

name: antimicrobial drug
description: A drug used to treat or prevent microbial infections.

name: antibacterial drug
description: A drug used to treat or prevent bacterial infections.

name: benzoate ester
description: Esters of benzoic acid or substituted benzoic acids.

name: hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion
description: Any monocarboxylic acid anion carrying at least one hydroxy substituent.

name: protein
description: A biological macromolecule minimally consisting of one polypeptide chain synthesized at the ribosome.

name: alicyclic ketone
description: A cyclic ketone in which the carbocyclic ring structure which may be saturated or unsaturated, but may not be a benzenoid or other aromatic system.

name: bile acid salt
description: A salt of a bile acid.

name: local anaesthetic
description: Any member of a group of drugs that reversibly inhibit the propagation of signals along nerves. Wide variations in potency, stability, toxicity, water-solubility and duration of action determine the route used for administration, e.g. topical, intravenous, epidural or spinal block.

name: lepton
description: Lepton is a fermion that does not experience the strong force (strong interaction). The term is derived from the Greek lambdaepsilonpitauomicronsigma (small, thin).

name: baryon
description: Baryon is a fermion that does experience the strong force (strong interaction). The term is derived from the Greek betaalpharhoupsilonsigma (heavy).

name: fermion
description: Particle of half-integer spin quantum number following Fermi-Dirac statistics. Fermions are named after Enrico Fermi.

name: subatomic particle
description: A particle smaller than an atom.

name: composite particle
description: A subatomic particle known to have substructure (i.e. consisting of smaller particles).

name: hadron
description: Hadron is a subatomic particle which experiences the strong force.

name: nuclear particle
description: A nucleus or any of its constituents in any of their energy states.

name: polyatomic entity
description: Any molecular entity consisting of more than one atom.

name: polyatomic ion
description: An ion consisting of more than one atom.

name: galactosylceramide
description: Any of the cerebrosides in which the monosaccharide head group is galactose.

name: carbonyl compound
description: Any compound containing the carbonyl group, C=O. The term is commonly used in the restricted sense of aldehydes and ketones, although it actually includes carboxylic acids and derivatives.

name: organic oxo compound
description: Organic compounds containing an oxygen atom, =O, doubly bonded to carbon or another element.

name: organochlorine compound
description: An organochlorine compound is a compound containing at least one carbon-chlorine bond.

name: chlorocarboxylic acid
description: A carboxylic acid containing at least one chloro group.

name: corticosteroid hormone
description: Any of a class of steroid hormones that are produced in the adrenal cortex.

name: phosphocholines
description: Any compound having phosphocholine as part of its structure.

name: biladienes
description: Compounds based on a biladiene skeleton.

name: ring assembly
description: Two or more cyclic systems (single rings or fused systems) which are directly joined to each other by double or single bonds are named ring assemblies when the number of such direct ring junctions is one less than the number of cyclic systems involved.

name: 3-hydroxy steroid
description: Any hydroxy steroid carrying a hydroxy group at position 3.

name: 3beta-hydroxy steroid
description: A 3-hydroxy steroid in which the 3-hydroxy substituent is in the  beta-position.

name: 20-oxo steroid
description: An oxo steroid carrying an oxo group at position 20.

name: cation
description: A monoatomic or polyatomic species having one or more elementary charges of the proton.

name: organochalcogen compound
description: An organochalcogen compound is a compound containing at least one carbon-chalcogen bond.

name: organooxygen compound
description: An organochalcogen compound containing at least one carbon-oxygen bond.

name: 7,8-dimethylisoalloxazine
description: A 7,8-dimethylbenzo[g]pteridine-2,4-dione that is  isoalloxazine substituted by methyl groups at positions 7 and 8.

name: mucopolysaccharide
description: Any of the group of polysaccharides composed of alternating units from uronic acids and glycosamines, and commonly partially esterified with sulfuric acid.

name: chondroitin sulfate
description: Any of a class of 10--60 kDa glycosaminoglycan sulfates, widely distributed in cartilage and other mammalian connective tissues.

name: acid
description: An acid is a molecular entity capable of donating a hydron (Bronsted acid) or capable of forming a covalent bond with an electron pair (Lewis acid).

name: heteroatomic molecular entity
description: A molecular entity consisting of two or more chemical elements.

name: halide
description: Any heteroatomic molecular entity that is a chemical compound of halogen with other chemical elements.

name: gamma-lactone
description: A lactone having a five-membered lactone ring.

name: carboxamide
description: An amide of a carboxylic acid, having the structure RC(=O)NR2. The term is used as a suffix in systematic name formation to denote the -C(=O)NH2 group including its carbon atom.

name: penicillanic acid
description: A penam that consists of 3,3-dimethyl-7-oxo-4-thia-1-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptane bearing a carboxy group at position 2 and having (2S,5R)-configuration.

name: carboacyl group
description: A carboacyl group is a group formed by loss of at least one OH from the carboxy group of a carboxylic acid.

name: plant hormone
description: A plant growth regulator that modulates the formation of stems, leaves and flowers, as well as the development and ripening of fruit. The term includes endogenous and non-endogenous compounds (e.g. active compounds produced by bacteria on the leaf surface) as well as semi-synthetic and fully synthetic compounds.

name: adrenergic agent
description: Any agent that acts on an adrenergic receptor or affects the life cycle of an adrenergic transmitter.

name: carbotricyclic compound
description: A carbopolyclic compound comprising of three carbocyclic rings.

name: anti-arrhythmia drug
description: A drug used for the treatment or prevention of cardiac arrhythmias. Anti-arrhythmia drugs may affect the polarisation-repolarisation phase of the action potential, its excitability or refractoriness, or impulse conduction or membrane responsiveness within cardiac fibres.

name: polypyrrole
description: A compound composed of two or more pyrrole units.

name: cardenolide glycoside
description: Any member of the class of cardenolides with glycosyl residues attached to position 3.

name: organonitrogen heterocyclic compound
description: Any organonitrogen compound containing a cyclic component with nitrogen and at least one other element as ring member atoms.

name: oxacycle
description: Any organic heterocyclic compound containing at least one ring oxygen atom.

name: cardiotonic drug
description: A drug that has a strengthening effect on the heart or that can increase cardiac output.

name: monohydroxypyridine
description: A hydroxypyridine carrying a single hydroxy substituent.

name: hydroxymethylpyridine
description: Any member of the class of  pyridines carrying a hydroxymethyl substituent at unspecified position.

name: DNA polymerase inhibitor
description: Any inhibitor of a DNA polymerase.

name: diazines
description: Any organic heterocyclic compound containing a benzene ring in which two of the C-H fragments have been replaced by isolobal nitrogens (the diazine parent structure).

name: cholinergic drug
description: Any drug used for its actions on cholinergic systems. Included here are agonists and antagonists, drugs that affect the life cycle of acetylcholine, and drugs that affect the survival of cholinergic neurons.

name: pyrimidone
description: A pyrimidine carrying one or more oxo substituents.

name: aminopyrimidine
description: A member of the class of  pyrimidines that is pyrimidine substituted by at least one amino group and its derivatives.

name: EC 1.9.3.1 (cytochrome c oxidase) inhibitor
description: An EC 1.9.3.* (oxidoreductase acting on donor heme group, oxygen as acceptor) inhibitor that interferes with the action of cytochrome c oxidase (EC 1.9.3.1).

name: membrane transport modulator
description: Any agent that affects the transport of molecular entities across a biological membrane.

name: sodium channel blocker
description: An agent that inhibits sodium influx through cell membranes.

name: carboxylic acid dianion
description: Any dianion containing at least one carboxy group.

name: anaesthetic
description: Substance which produces loss of feeling or sensation.

name: general anaesthetic
description: Substance that produces loss of consciousness.

name: corticotropin
description: A polypeptide hormone produced and secreted by the pituitary gland comprising 39 amino acid residues coupled in a linear sequence. The N-terminal 24-amino acid segment is identical in all species and contains the adrenocorticotrophic activity. Corticotropin stimulates the cortex of the adrenal gland and boosts the synthesis of corticosteroids, mainly glucocorticoids but also sex steroids (androgens). It is used in the treatment of certain neurological disorders such as infantile spasms and multiple sclerosis, and diagnostically to investigate adrenocortical insufficiency.

name: methylbenzene
description: Any alkylbenzene that is benzene substituted with one or more methyl groups.

name: alkylbenzene
description: A  monocyclic arene that is benzene substituted with one or more alkyl groups.

name: apolipoprotein
description: Protein component on the surface of lipoprotein.

name: inclusion compound
description: A complex in which one component (the host) forms a cavity or, in the case of a crystal, a crystal lattice containing spaces in the shape of long tunnels or channels in which molecular entities of a second chemical species (the guest) are located. There is no covalent bonding between guest and host, the attraction being generally due to van der Waals forces.

name: clathrate compound
description: Inclusion compound in which the guest molecule is in a cage formed by the host molecule or by a lattice of host molecules.

name: Bronsted acid
description: A molecular entity capable of donating a hydron to an acceptor (Bronsted base).

name: Bronsted base
description: A molecular entity capable of accepting a hydron from a donor (Bronsted acid).

name: Lewis base
description: A molecular entity able to provide a pair of electrons and thus capable of forming a covalent bond with an electron-pair acceptor (Lewis acid), thereby producing a Lewis adduct.

name: growth regulator
description: Any chemical substance that inhibits the life-cycle of an organism.

name: pyrimidines
description: Any compound having a pyrimidine as part of its structure.

name: dihydrogenphosphate
description: A monovalent inorganic anion that consists of phosphoric acid in which one of the three OH groups has been deprotonated.

name: (R)-lactic acid
description: An optically active form of lactic acid having (R)-configuration.

name: (S)-lactic acid
description: An optically active form of lactic acid having (S)-configuration.

name: (R)-amphetamine
description: A 1-phenylpropan-2-amine that has R configuration.

name: hydrogenphosphate
description: A phosphate ion that is the conjugate base of dihydrogenphosphate.

name: (S)-amphetamine
description: A 1-phenylpropan-2-amine that has S configuration.

name: digoxin
description: A  cardenolide glycoside that is digitoxin beta-hydroxylated at C-12. A cardiac glycoside extracted from the foxglove plant, Digitalis lanata, it is used to control ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation and in the management of congestive heart failure with atrial fibrillation, but the margin between toxic and therapeutic doses is small.

name: paracetamol
description: A member of the class of phenols that is 4-aminophenol in which one of the hydrogens attached to the amino group has been replaced by an acetyl group.

name: L-tyrosinal
description: An amino aldehyde that is L-tyrosine in which the carboxy group has undergone formal redution to give the corrresponding aldehyde

name: asbestos
description: Fibrous incombustible mineral composed of magnesium and calcium silicates with or without other elements.

name: mineral
description: In general, a mineral is a chemical substance that is normally crystalline formed and has been formed as a result of geological processes. The term also includes metamict substances (naturally occurring, formerly crystalline substances whose crystallinity has been destroyed by ionising radiation) and can include naturally occurring amorphous substances that have never been crystalline ('mineraloids') such as georgite and calciouranoite as well as substances formed by the action of geological processes on bigenic compounds ('biogenic minerals').

name: solvent
description: A liquid that can dissolve other substances (solutes) without any change in their chemical composition.

name: urate anion
description: An organic anion obtained by removal of at least one proton from any uric acid.

name: 2-aminooctadecene-1,3-diol
description: An aminodiol composed of any octadecene having hydroxy functional groups at positions 1 and 3 and an amino substituent at position 2.

name: 2-aminooctadec-4-ene-1,3-diol
description: A 2-aminooctadecene-1,3-diol having its double bond at position 4.

name: (2R,3S)-2-aminooctadec-4-ene-1,3-diol
description: A 2-aminooctadec-4-ene-1,3-diol having (2R,3S)-configuration.

name: L-erythro-sphingosine
description: A (2R,3S)-2-aminooctadec-4-ene-1,3-diol in which the double bond has E geochemistry.

name: acetate ester
description: Any carboxylic ester where the carboxylic acid component is acetic acid.

name: 3-oxo steroid
description: Any oxo steroid where an oxo substituent is located at position 3.

name: indicator
description: Anything used in a scientific experiment to indicate the presence of a substance or quality, change in a body, etc.

name: photosensitizing agent
description: A chemical compound that can be excited by light of a specific wavelength and subsequently transfer energy to a chosen reactant. This is commonly molecular oxygen within a cancer tissue, which is converted to (highly rective) singlet state oxygen. This rapidly reacts with any nearby biomolecules, ultimately killing the cancer cells.

name: 3-oxo-Delta(4) steroid
description: A 3-oxo steroid conjugated to a C=C double bond at the alpha,beta position.

name: protein synthesis inhibitor
description: A compound, usually an anti-bacterial agent or a toxin, which inhibits the synthesis of a protein.

name: disinfectant
description: An antimicrobial agent that is applied to non-living objects to destroy harmful microorganisms or to inhibit their activity.

name: disulfide
description: Compounds of structure RSSR'.

name: polar solvent
description: A solvent that is composed of polar molecules. Polar solvents can dissolve ionic compounds or ionisable covalent compounds.

name: protic solvent
description: A polar solvent that is capable of acting as a hydron (proton) donor.

name: protophilic solvent
description: Solvent that is capable of acting as a hydron (proton) acceptor.

name: amphiprotic solvent
description: Self-ionizing solvent possessing both characteristics of Bronsted acids and bases.

name: imidic acid
description: Compounds derived from oxoacids RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l =/= 0) by replacing =O by =NR; thus tautomers of amides. In organic chemistry an unspecified imidic acid is generally a carboximidic acid, RC(=NR)(OH).

name: isourea
description: A carboximidic acid that is the imidic acid tautomer of urea, H2NC(=NH)OH, and its hydrocarbyl derivatives.

name: antiparkinson drug
description: A drug used in the treatment of Parkinson's disease.

name: dopaminergic agent
description: A drug used for its effects on dopamine receptors, on the life cycle of dopamine, or on the survival of dopaminergic neurons.

name: agonist
description: Substance which binds to cell receptors normally responding to naturally occurring substances and which produces a response of its own.

name: antagonist
description: Substance that attaches to and blocks cell receptors that normally bind naturally occurring substances.

name: aluminosilicate mineral
description: Silicate minerals that contain aluminium, silicon, and oxygen, together with other ions. They are a major component of clay minerals.

name: cholinergic antagonist
description: Any drug that binds to but does not activate cholinergic receptors, thereby blocking the actions of acetylcholine or cholinergic agonists.

name: thiazoles
description: An azole in which the five-membered heterocyclic aromatic skeleton contains a N atom and one S atom.

name: hormone antagonist
description: A chemical substance which inhibits the function of the endocrine glands, the biosynthesis of their secreted hormones, or the action of hormones upon their specific sites.

name: prostaglandin antagonist
description: A compound that inhibits the action of prostaglandins.

name: heteroarenecarbaldehyde
description: An aldehyde in which a formyl group is located on a heteroarene.

name: anti-asthmatic drug
description: A drug used to treat asthma.

name: dopa
description: A hydroxyphenylalanine carrying hydroxy substituents at positions 3 and 4 of the benzene ring.

name: D-dopa
description: The D-enantiomer of dopa.

name: organic amino compound
description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.

name: sex hormone
description: Any hormone that is responsible for controlling sexual characteristics and reproductive function.

name: androgen
description: A sex hormone that stimulates or controls the development and maintenance of masculine characteristics in vertebrates by binding to androgen receptors.

name: estrogen
description: A hormone that stimulates or controls the development and maintenance of female sex characteristics in mammals by binding to oestrogen receptors. The oestrogens are named for their importance in the oestrous cycle. The oestrogens that occur naturally in the body, notably estrone, estradiol, estriol, and estetrol are steroids. Other compounds with oestrogenic activity are produced by plants (phytoestrogens) and fungi (mycoestrogens); synthetic compounds with oestrogenic activity are known as xenoestrogens.

name: keratolytic drug
description: A drug that softens, separates, and causes desquamation of the cornified epithelium or horny layer of skin. Keratolytic drugs are used to expose mycelia of infecting fungi or to treat corns, warts, and certain other skin diseases.

name: dermatologic drug
description: A drug used to treat or prevent skin disorders or for the routine care of skin.

name: P450 inhibitor
description: An enzyme inhibitor that interferes with the activity of cytochrome P450 involved in catalysis of organic substances.

name: hematologic agent
description: Drug that acts on blood and blood-forming organs and those that affect the hemostatic system.

name: anticoagulant
description: An agent that prevents blood clotting.

name: prodrug
description: A compound that, on administration, must undergo chemical conversion by metabolic processes before becoming the pharmacologically active drug for which it is a prodrug.

name: protective agent
description: Synthetic or natural substance which is given to prevent a disease or disorder or are used in the process of treating a disease or injury due to a poisonous agent.

name: GABA modulator
description: A substance that does not act as agonist or antagonist but does affect the gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor-ionophore complex. GABA-A receptors appear to have at least three allosteric sites at which modulators act: a site at which benzodiazepines act by increasing the opening frequency of gamma-aminobutyric acid-activated chloride channels; a site at which barbiturates act to prolong the duration of channel opening; and a site at which some steroids may act.

name: onium cation
description: Mononuclear cations derived by addition of a hydron to a mononuclear parent hydride of the pnictogen, chalcogen and halogen families.

name: proteinogenic amino-acid side-chain group
description: A univalent organyl group obtained by cleaving the bond from C-2 to the side chain of a proteinogenic amino-acid.

name: cholestanoid
description: Any steroid based on a cholestane skeleton and its derivatives.

name: lipoprotein cholesterol
description: Cholesterol esters and free cholesterol which are contained in or bound to lipoproteins.

name: probe
description: A role played by a molecular entity used to study the microscopic environment.

name: platelet aggregation inhibitor
description: A drug or agent which antagonizes or impairs any mechanism leading to blood platelet aggregation, whether during the phases of activation and shape change or following the dense-granule release reaction and stimulation of the prostaglandin-thromboxane system.

name: bipyridines
description: Compounds containing a bipyridine group.

name: vasoconstrictor agent
description: Drug used to cause constriction of the blood vessels.

name: butenolide
description: A gamma-lactone that consists of a 2-furanone skeleton and its substituted derivatives.

name: alkyl alcohol
description: An aliphatic alcohol in which the aliphatic alkane chain is substituted by a hydroxy group at unspecified position.

name: cyclooxygenase 2 inhibitor
description: A cyclooxygenase inhibitor that interferes with the action of cyclooxygenase 2.

name: cyclooxygenase 1 inhibitor
description: A cyclooxygenase inhibitor that interferes with the action of cyclooxygenase 1.

name: EC 1.5.1.3 (dihydrofolate reductase) inhibitor
description: An EC 1.5.1.* (oxidoreductase acting on donor CH-NH group, NAD(+) or NADP(+) as acceptor) inhibitor that interferes with the action of dihydrofolate reductase (EC 1.5.1.3).

name: reproductive control drug
description: A substance used either in the prevention or facilitation of pregnancy.

name: abortifacient
description: A chemical substance that interrupts pregnancy after implantation.

name: nutraceutical
description: A product in capsule, tablet or liquid form that provide essential nutrients, such as a vitamin, an essential mineral, a protein, an herb, or similar nutritional substance.

name: immunomodulator
description: Biologically active substance whose activity affects or plays a role in the functioning of the immune system.

name: corticosteroid
description: A natural or synthetic analogue of the hormones secreted by the adrenal gland.

name: organic molecular entity
description: Any molecular entity that contains carbon.

name: genotoxin
description: A role played by a chemical compound to induce direct or indirect DNA damage. Such damage can potentially lead to the formation of a malignant tumour, but DNA damage does not lead inevitably to the creation of cancerous cells.

name: carcinogenic agent
description: A role played by a chemical compound which is known to  induce a process of carcinogenesis  by corrupting  normal cellular pathways, leading to the acquistion of tumoral capabilities.

name: allergen
description: A chemical compound, or part thereof, which causes the onset of an allergic reaction by interacting with any of the molecular pathways involved in an allergy.

name: teratogenic agent
description: A role played by a chemical compound  in biological systems with adverse consequences in embryo developments, leading to birth defects, embryo death or altered development, growth retardation and functional defect.

name: role
description: A role is particular behaviour which a material entity may exhibit.

name: hepatotoxic agent
description: A role played by a chemical compound exihibiting itself through the ability to induce damage to the liver in animals.

name: neurotoxin
description: A poison that interferes with the functions of the nervous system.

name: serotonin uptake inhibitor
description: A compound that specifically inhibits the reuptake of serotonin in the brain. This increases the serotonin concentration in the synaptic cleft which then activates serotonin receptors to a greater extent.

name: non-covalently-bound molecular entity
description: Systems consisting of two or more molecular entities held together by non-covalent interactions.

name: primary amino compound
description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one hydrogen atom by an organyl group.

name: secondary amino compound
description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing two hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.

name: tertiary amino compound
description: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing three hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.

name: dopamine uptake inhibitor
description: A dopaminergic agent that blocks the transport of dopamine into axon terminals or into storage vesicles within terminals. Most of the adrenergic uptake inhibitors also inhibit dopamine uptake.

name: hormone receptor modulator
description: A drug that modulates the function of the endocrine glands, the biosynthesis of their secreted hormones, or the action of hormones upon their specific sites.

name: chemical role
description: A role played by the molecular entity or part thereof within a chemical context.

name: dipolar compound
description: An  organic molecule that is electrically neutral carrying a positive and a negative charge in one of its major canonical descriptions. In most dipolar compounds the charges are delocalized; however the term is also applied to species where this is not the case.

name: acenes
description: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons consisting of fused benzene rings in a rectilinear arrangement and their substitution derivatives.

name: tetracenes
description: Compounds containing a tetracene skeleton.

name: penicillinate anion
description: Any anion formed by loss of a proton from the carboxy group of a penicillin.

name: GABA agent
description: A substance, such as agonists, antagonists, degradation or uptake inhibitors, depleters, precursors, and modulators of receptor function, used for its pharmacological actions on GABAergic systems.

name: organodiyl group
description: Any organic substituent group, regardless of functional type, having two free valences at carbon atom(s).

name: biotins
description: Compounds containing a biotin (5-[(3aS,4S,6aR)-2-oxohexahydro-1H-thieno[3,4-d]imidazol-4-yl]pentanoic acid) skeleton.

name: enone
description: An alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone of general formula R(1)R(2)C=CR(3)-C(=O)R(4) (R(4) =/= H) in which the C=O function is conjugated to a C=C double bond at the alpha,beta position.

name: alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone
description: A ketone of general formula R(1)R(2)C=CR(3)-C(=O)R(4) (R(4) =/= H) or R(1)C#C-C(=O)R(2) (R(2) =/= H) in which the ketonic C=O function is conjugated to an unsaturated C-C bond at the alpha,beta position.

name: methoxide
description: An organic anion that is the conjugate base of methanol.

name: biochemical role
description: A biological role played by the molecular entity or part thereof within a biochemical context.

name: aetiopathogenetic role
description: A role played by the molecular entity or part thereof which causes the development of a pathological process.

name: pharmacological role
description: A biological role which describes how a drug interacts within a biological system and how the interactions affect its medicinal properties.

name: ligand
description: Any molecule or ion capable of binding to a central metal atom to form coordination complexes.

name: pharmaceutical
description: Any substance introduced into a living organism with therapeutic or diagnostic purpose.

name: apatite
description: A phosphate mineral with the general formula Ca5(PO4)3X where X = OH, F or Cl.

name: hydroxylapatite
description: A phosphate mineral with the formula Ca5(PO4)3(OH).

name: oxyketone
description: A compound with the general formula R2C=O (R=/=H) where one or more of the R groups contains an oxy (-O-) group.

name: alpha-oxyketone
description: An oxyketone with the general formula R2C(=O) (R=/=H) where one or more of the R groups contains an oxy (-O-) group and the oxy and carbonyl groups are bonded to the same carbon atom.

name: galactolipid
description: A glycolipid and which the glyco component is specified as galactosyl.

name: epitope
description: The biological role played by a material entity when bound by a receptor of the adaptive immune system. Specific site on an antigen to which an antibody binds.

name: isocyanates
description: Organonitrogen compounds that are derivatives of isocyanic acid; compounds containing the isocyanate functional group -N=C=O (as opposed to the cyanate group, -O-C#N).

name: polyanionic macromolecule
description: A polymer carrying multiple negative charges.

name: ionic macromolecule
description: A macromolecule containing ionic groups.

name: antidiarrhoeal drug
description: Any drug found useful in the symptomatic treatment of diarrhoea.

name: gastrointestinal drug
description: A drug used for its effects on the gastrointestinal system, e.g. controlling gastric acidity, regulating gastrointestinal motility and water flow, and improving digestion.

name: heterocyclic compound
description: A cyclic compound having as ring members atoms of at least two different elements.

name: L-dopa zwitterion
description: An amino acid zwitterion obtained from the transfer of a proton from the carboxy group to the amino group of L-dopa. Major microspecies at pH 7.3.

name: biotinate
description: Conjugate base of biotin arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.

name: chondroitin D-glucuronate anion
description: Anionic form of chondroitin D-glucuronate arising from deprotonation of the carboxylic acid groups of the repeating units; major species at pH 7.3.

name: barbiturate(2-)
description: Dianion of barbituric acid arising from deprotonation at the N-1 and C-5 positions.

name: sphingosine(1+)
description: The cationic sphingoid resulting from the protonation of the amino group of sphingosine.

name: 6-aminopenicillanic acid zwitterion
description: Zwitterionic form of 6-aminopenicillanic acid arising from migration of a proton from the carboxy group to the 6-amino group; major species at pH 7.3.

name: psychosine(1+)
description: The ammonium ion resulting from the protonation of the amino group of psychosine.

name: bilirubin(2-)
description: A dicarboxylic acid dianion obtained by deprotonation of the two carboxy groups of bilirubin; major species at pH 7.3.

name: D-phenylalanine zwitterion
description: A D-alpha-amino acid zwitterion that is D-phenylalanine in which a proton has been transferred from the carboxy group to the amino group. It is the major species at pH 7.3.

name: riboflavin(1-)
description: An organic anion that is the conjugate base of riboflavin resulting from the removal of a proton from the nitrogen at position 3 (between the two carbonyl groups). Major microspecies at pH 7.3.

name: carbon monoxide(1+)
description: Conjugate acid of carbon monoxide arising from protonation of the carbon; major species at pH 7.3.

name: L-phenylalanine zwitterion
description: An amino acid zwitterion arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-phenylalanine; major species at pH 7.3.

name: (2S)-2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion
description: A hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion where the hydroxy group is placed at position 2 (alpha to the carboxy group) and has (S)-stereochemistry; major species at pH 7.3.

name: homocystine zwitterion
description: Dizwitterionic form of homocystine arising from transfer of two protons from the carboxy to the amino groups; major species at pH 7.3.

name: (2R)-2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion
description: A hydroxy monocarboxylic acid anion where the hydroxy group is placed at position 2 (alpha to the carboxy group) and has (R)-stereochemistry; major species at pH 7.3.

name: L-tyrosine zwitterion
description: An amino acid zwitterion arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-tyrosine; major species at pH 7.3.

name: D-tyrosine zwitterion
description: A D-alpha-amino acid zwitterion that is D-tyrosine in which a proton has been transferred from the carboxy group to the amino group. It is the major species at pH 7.3.

name: cationic amino-acid residue
description: An amino-acid residue protonated on nitrogen.

name: organophosphate oxoanion
description: An organic phosphoric acid derivative in which one or more oxygen atoms of the phosphate group(s) has been deprotonated.

name: short-chain fatty acid anion
description: Any fatty acid anion obtained by removal of a proton from the carboxy group of a short-chain fatty acid (chain length of less than C6).

name: saturated fatty acid anion
description: Any fatty acid anion in which there is no C-C unsaturation.

name: organosulfate oxoanion
description: An organic anion of general formula RS(=O)2O(-) where R is an organyl group.

name: piperidinium
description: The conjugate acid of piperidine; major species at pH 7.3.

name: biomarker
description: A substance used as an indicator  of a biological state.

name: hapten
description: Any substance capable of eliciting an immune response only when attached to a large carrier such as a protein. Examples include dinitrophenols; oligosaccharides; peptides; and heavy metals.

name: linear tetrapyrrole anion
description: An organic anion arising from deprotonation of a acyclic tetrapyrrole compound.

name: insulin (human)
description: An insulin that is produced in the pancreas and involved in regulating the metabolism of carbohydrates (particularly glucose) and fats. Commonly thought of as a protein, it consists of two peptide chains, one containing 21 amino acid residues and the other containing 30; the chains are joined together by 2 disulfide bonds. Recombinant insulin is identical to human insulin, but is synthesised by inserting the human insulin gene into E. coli, which then produces insulin for human use. It is used in the treatment of type I and type II diabetes.

name: DNA synthesis inhibitor
description: Any substance that inhibits the synthesis of DNA.

name: sapropterin
description: A tetrahydropterin that is 2-amino-5,6,7,8-tetrahydropteridin-4(3H)-one in which a hydrogen at position 6 is substituted by a 1,2-dihydroxypropyl group (6R,1'R,2'S-enantiomer).

name: phosphoric acids
description: Compounds containing one or more phosphoric acid units.

name: pyridoxal 5'-phosphate(2-)
description: The dianion resulting from the removal of two protons from the phosphate group of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate.

name: nucleophilic reagent
description: A reagent that forms a bond to its reaction partner (the electrophile) by donating both bonding electrons.

name: L-alpha-amino acid anion
description: Conjugate base of an L-alpha-amino acid arising from deprotonation of the C-1 carboxy group.

name: L-alpha-amino acid zwitterion
description: Zwitterionic form of an L-alpha-amino acid having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated amino group.

name: D-alpha-amino acid zwitterion
description: Zwitterionic form of a D-alpha-amino acid having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated amino group.

name: chemical substance
description: A chemical substance is a portion of matter of constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same type or of different types.

name: mixture
description: A mixture is a chemical substance composed of multiple molecules, at least two of which are of a different kind.

name: polymer
description: A polymer is a mixture, which is composed of macromolecules of different kinds and which may be differentiated by composition, length, degree of branching etc..

name: cocaine(1+)
description: The conjugate base of cocaine arising from protonation of the tertiary amino group; major species at pH 7.3.

name: ionic polymer
description: An ionic polymer is a polymer, composed of ionic macromolecules.

name: monovalent inorganic cation
description: An atom or small molecule with a positive charge that does not contain carbon in covalent linkage, with a valency of one.

name: peptide zwitterion
description: Zwitterionic form of any peptide where, in general, the amino terminus is positively charged and the carboxy terminus is negatively charged.

name: flavin(1-)
description: Flavin protonated to pH 7.3

name: NMDA receptor antagonist
description: Any substance that inhibits the action of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors. They tend to induce a state known as dissociative anesthesia, marked by catalepsy, amnesia, and analgesia, while side effects can include hallucinations, nightmares, and confusion. Due to their psychotomimetic effects, many NMDA receptor antagonists are used as recreational drugs.

name: isotretinoin
description: A retinoic acid that is all-trans-retinoic acid in which the double bond which is alpha,beta- to the carboxy group is isomerised to Z configuration. A synthetic retinoid, it is used for the treatment of severe cases of acne and other skin diseases.

name: excitatory amino acid antagonist
description: Any substance which inhibits the action of receptors for excitatory amino acids.

name: adjuvant
description: Any pharmacological or immunological agent that modifies the effect of other agents such as drugs or vaccines while having few if any direct effects when given by itself.

name: tubulin modulator
description: Any substance that interacts with tubulin to inhibit or promote polymerisation of microtubules.

name: D-alpha-amino acid anion
description: Any alpha-amino acid anion in which the parent amino acid has D-configuration.

name: racemate
description: A racemate is an equimolar mixture of a pair of enantiomers.

name: keratan sulfate
description: A sulfated glycosaminoglycan, a linear polymer that consists of the repeating disaccharide  [3)-beta-Gal-(1->4)-beta-GlcNAc-(1->] and containing sulfo groups located at random positions.

name: ketamine
description: A member of the class of cyclohexanones in which one of the hydrogens at position 2 is substituted by a 2-chlorophenyl group, while the other is substituted by a methylamino group.

name: C21-steroid
description: A steroid that has a structure based on a 21-carbon (pregnane) skeleton. Note that individual examples may have ring substituents at other positions and/or contain double bonds, aromatic A-rings, expanded/contracted rings etc., so the formula and mass may vary from that given for the generic structure.

name: C4-dicarboxylate
description: A dicarboxylate that contains four carbon atoms.

name: polyanionic polymer
description: A polymer, composed of polyanion macromolecules.

name: steroid saponin
description: Any saponin derived from a hydroxysteroid.

name: microtubule-destabilising agent
description: Any substance that interacts with tubulin to inhibit polymerisation of microtubules.

name: polar amino acid zwitterion
description: Zwitterionic form of a polar amino acid having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated amino group.

name: allelochemical
description: A class of secondary metabolites developed by many plants to influence the behaviour, growth or survival of herbivores, and thus acting as a defence against herbivory.

name: signalling molecule
description: A molecular messenger in which the molecule is specifically involved in transmitting information between cells. Such molecules are released from the cell sending the signal, cross over the gap between cells by diffusion, and interact with specific receptors in another cell, triggering a response in that cell by activating a series of enzyme controlled reactions which lead to changes inside the cell.

name: anionic phospholipid
description: Any organophosphate oxoanion that is a negatively charged phospholipid, e.g. phosphatidylserine(1-), phosphatidate(2-), phosphatidylglycerol(1-).

name: aromatic ester
description: An ester where the ester linkage is bonded directly to an aromatic system.

name: tyrosine derivative
description: An amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of tyrosine at the amino group or the carboxy group, any substitution of phenyl hydrogens, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of tyrosine by a heteroatom. The definition normally excludes peptides containing tyrosine residues.

name: fuel additive
description: Any additive that enhances the efficiency of fuel.

name: glycosylceramide
description: A ceramide compound formed by the replacement of the glycosidic hydroxy group of a cyclic form of a monosaccharide (or derivative) by a ceramide group.

name: 1,3-thiazolium cation
description: An organic cation resulting from protonation or quaternisation at the 3-position of any 1,3-thiazole.

name: glycosyl compound
description: A carbohydrate derivative arising formally from the elimination of water from a glycosidic hydroxy group and an H atom bound to an oxygen, carbon, nitrogen or sulfur atom of a separate entity.

name: oxidising agent
description: A substance that removes electrons from another reactant in a redox reaction.

name: carbohydrate derivative
description: Any organooxygen compound derived from a carbohydrate by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by an amino group, a thiol group or similar heteroatomic groups. The term also includes derivatives of these compounds.

name: EC 3.1.3.1 (alkaline phosphatase) inhibitor
description: An EC 3.1.3.* (phosphoric monoester hydrolase) inhibitor that interferes with the action of alkaline phosphatase (EC 3.1.3.1).

name: carbohydrate acid derivative
description: A carbohydrate derivative that is formally obtained from a carbohydrate acid.

name: sulfur-containing amino-acid anion
description: A sulfur-containing amino acid whose alpha-carboxylic acid group is ionized (not protonated).

name: branched-chain amino-acid anion
description: A branched-chain amino acid whose alpha-carboxylic acid group is ionized.

name: aromatic amino-acid anion
description: An aromatic amino acid whose alpha-carboxylic acid group is ionized (non-protonated).

name: EC 3.6.3.9 (Na(+)/K(+)-transporting ATPase) inhibitor
description: An EC 3.6.3.* (acid anhydride hydrolase catalysing transmembrane movement of substances) inhibitor that interferes with the action of  Na(+)/K(+)-transporting ATPase (EC 3.6.3.9).

name: carbohydrate acid derivative anion
description: A carboxylic acid anion resulting from the deprotonation of the carboxy group of a carbohydrate acid derivative.

name: food additive
description: Any substance which is added to food to preserve or enhance its flavour and/or appearance.

name: food acidity regulator
description: A food additive that is used to change or otherwise control the acidity or alkalinity of foods. They may be acids, bases, neutralising agents or buffering agents.

name: EC 1.3.1.43 (arogenate dehydrogenase) inhibitor
description: An EC 1.3.1.* (oxidoreductase acting on CH-CH group of donor, NAD(+) or NADP(+) as acceptor) inhibitor that interferes with the action of arogenate dehydrogenase (EC 1.3.1.43).

name: biaryl
description: An organic aromatic compound whose structure contains two aromatic rings or ring systems, joined to each other by a single bond.

name: flour treatment agent
description: A food additive which is added to flour or dough to improve baking quality and/or colour.

name: sphingomyelin
description: Any of a class of phospholipids in which the amino group of a sphingoid base is in amide linkage with one of several fatty acids, while the terminal hydroxy group of the sphingoid base is esterified to phosphorylcholine.

name: C21-steroid hormone
description: A steroid compound with a structure based on a 21-carbon (pregnane) skeleton that acts as a hormone.

name: one-carbon compound
description: An organic molecular entity containing a single carbon atom (C1).

name: organic acid
description: Any organic molecular entity that is acidic and contains carbon in covalent linkage.

name: cationic group
description: A group that carries an overall positive charge.

name: anionic group
description: A group that carries an overall negative charge.

name: organic cationic group
description: A cationic group that contains carbon.

name: organic anionic group
description: An anionic group that contains carbon.

name: anionic amino-acid residue
description: An amino-acid residue carrying an overall negative charge.

name: poison
description: Any substance that causes disturbance to organisms by chemical reaction or other activity on the molecular scale, when a sufficient quantity is absorbed by the organism.

name: antimitotic
description: Any compound that inhibits cell division (mitosis).

name: lipoprotein
description: A clathrate complex consisting of a lipid enwrapped in a protein host without covalent binding in such a way that the complex has a hydrophilic outer surface consisting of all the protein and the polar ends of any phospholipids.

name: EC 1.13.11.33 (arachidonate 15-lipoxygenase) inhibitor
description: A lipoxygenase inhibitor that interferes with the action of arachidonate 15-lipoxygenase (EC 1.13.11.33).

name: EC 3.1.1.3 (triacylglycerol lipase) inhibitor
description: Any EC 3.1.1.* (carboxylic ester hydrolase) inhibitor that inhibits the action of triacylglycerol lipase (EC 3.1.1.3).

name: anti-asthmatic agent
description: Any compound that has anti-asthmatic effects.

name: polysaccharide derivative
description: A carbohydrate derivative that is any derivative of a polysaccharide.

name: food preservative
description: Substances which are added to food in order to prevent decomposition caused by  microbial growth or by undesirable chemical changes.

name: antimicrobial food preservative
description: A food preservative which prevents decomposition of food by preventing the growth of fungi or bacteria. In European countries, E-numbers for permitted food preservatives are from E200 to E299, divided into sorbates (E200-209), benzoates (E210-219), sulfites (E220-229), phenols and formates (E230-239), nitrates (E240-259), acetates (E260-269), lactates (E270-279), propionates (E280-289) and others (E290-299).

name: primary ammonium ion
description: An ammonium ion derivative resulting from the protonation of the nitrogen atom of a primary amino compound. Major species at pH 7.3.

name: C4-dicarboxylic acid
description: Any dicarboxylic acid that contains four carbon atoms.

name: antidyskinesia agent
description: Any compound which can be used to treat or alleviate the symptoms of dyskinesia.

name: L-dopa(1-)
description: A L-alpha-amino acid anion which is the conjugate base of L-dopa, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group: major species at pH 7.3.

name: anti-inflammatory agent
description: Any compound that has anti-inflammatory effects.

name: azole
description: Any monocyclic heteroarene consisting of a five-membered ring containing nitrogen. Azoles can also contain one or more other non-carbon atoms, such as nitrogen, sulfur or oxygen.

name: EC 2.* (transferase) inhibitor
description: An enzyme inhibitor that inhibits the action of a transferase (EC 2.*)

name: tetracycline(1-)
description: An organic anion that is the conjugate base of tetracycline obtained by deprotonation of the two enolic hydroxy groups and protonation of the tertiary amino group.

name: organic molecule
description: Any molecule that consists of at least one carbon atom as part of the electrically neutral entity.

name: exopolysaccharide
description: A biomacromolecule composed of carbohydrate residues which is secreted by a microorganism into the surrounding environment.

name: EC 1.11.1.11 (L-ascorbate peroxidase) inhibitor
description: An  EC 1.11.1.* (peroxidases) inhibitor that inhibits the action of L-ascorbate peroxidase (EC 1.11.1.11).

name: plant activator
description: Any compound that protects plants by activating their defence mechanisms.

name: EC 3.6.* (hydrolases acting on acid anhydrides) inhibitor
description: Any hydrolase inhibitor that interferes with the action of a hydrolase which acts on acid anhydrides (EC 3.6.*.*).

name: cyclooxygenase 3 inhibitor
description: A cyclooxygenase inhibitor that interferes with the action of cyclooxygenase 3.

name: erythrose 4-phosphate/phosphoenolpyruvate family amino acid
description: An L-alpha-amino acid which is biosynthesised from erythrose 4-phosphate and phosphoenolpyruvate (i.e. phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan). A closed class.

name: antifolate
description: An antimetabolite that impairs the action of folic acids

name: cardenolides
description: Any steroid lactone that is a  C23 steroid with a five-membered lactone ring at C-17 and its substituted derivatives. They form the aglycone constituents of cardiac glycosides.

name: astringent
description: A compound that causes the contraction of body tissues, typically used to reduce bleeding from minor abrasions.

name: heteroaryl hydroxy compound
description: Any organic aromatic compound having one or more hydroxy groups attached to a heteroarene ring.

name: excipient
description: A generally pharmacologically inactive substance that is formulated with the active ingredient of a medication.

name: EC 1.11.1.* (peroxidases) inhibitor
description: An EC 1.11.* (oxidoreductase acting on peroxide as donors) inhibitor that interferes with the action of any of the peroxidases (EC 1.11.1.*).

name: EC 6.3.* (C-N bond-forming ligase) inhibitor
description: A ligase inhibitor that interferes with the action of a C-N bond-forming ligase (EC 6.3.*.*).

name: EC 6.* (ligase) inhibitor
description: Any enzyme inhibitor that interferes with the action of a ligase (EC 6.*.*.*). Ligases are enzymes that catalyse the joining of two molecules with concomitant hydrolysis of the diphosphate bond in ATP or a similar triphosphate.

name: eukaryotic metabolite
description: Any  metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in eukaryotes, the taxon that include members of the fungi, plantae and animalia kingdoms.

name: animal metabolite
description: Any eukaryotic metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in animals that include diverse creatures from sponges, insects to mammals.

name: mammalian metabolite
description: Any animal metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in mammals.

name: B vitamin
description: Any member of the group of eight water-soluble vitamins originally thought to be a single compound (vitamin B) that play important roles in cell metabolism. The group comprises of vitamin B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7, B9, and B12 (Around 20 other compounds were once thought to be B vitamins but are no longer classified as such).

name: mouse metabolite
description: Any mammalian metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in a mouse (Mus musculus).

name: Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite
description: Any  fungal metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).

name: prokaryotic metabolite
description: Any metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in prokaryotes, the taxon that include members of domains such as the bacteria and archaea.

name: aromatic amino-acid zwitterion

description: Raw goat milk.

name: cow milk (raw)
description: Raw cow milk.

name: shrimp paste
description: definition: Shrimp paste or shrimp sauce is a fermented condiment commonly used in Southeast Asian, Northeastern South Asian and Southern Chinese cuisines.

name: food (raw)
description: A food product that is raw.

name: fish product (unspecified species)
description: A fish product is a home-made or commercially produced or retail or wholesale product containing substantial amounts of freshwater or saltwater fish and/or shellfish flesh. Note that this category should avoid items that mention a particular species of fish or shellfish.

name: refined or partially-refined food product (us cfr)
description: Extract, concentrate or isolate derived from a food source through one or more refining steps (see *EXTRACT, CONCENTRATE OR ISOLATE OF PLANT OR ANIMAL*) and marketed as such. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

name: multicomponent meal (us cfr)
description: A multiple-component food product typically containing a protein source, a vegetable, and a potato, rice or cereal-based component packaged to be served after heating, either as separate items or courses or mixed as recipe components; see 21 CFR 102.26, 102.28 and 104.47 for nutritional quality guidelines.

name: milk or milk product (us cfr)
description: Milk in all forms, milk-based beverage, cultured milk product, or milk or milk product analog. Index infant formula under *MEAL REPLACEMENT*.

name: dairy product (us cfr)
description: Milk, a product derived from milk, or a dairy product analog; includes cheese and frozen dairy desserts. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

name: prepared food product (us cfr)
description: Food product that is 1) ready or nearly ready for consumption; 2) usually a composite of several foods or ingredients that often belong to distinct product types; 3) usually formulated, mixed and partially or fully cooked. Prepared foods often undergo several of the processes listed in *F. EXTENT OF HEAT TREATMENT* and *H. TREATMENT APPLIED*; these factors should be carefully considered in indexing. The classification of prepared food products emphasizes consumption characteristics. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

name: stew or hash (us cfr)
description: Prepared dish consisting of a mixture of meat, poultry or seafood with one or more vegetables and possibly other ingredients. In contrast to soups, which are liquid or semiliquid, stews are thickened or have a larger proportion of solid ingredients.

name: meat, poultry, seafood or related product (us cfr)
description: Products of the flesh of animals. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

name: beverage (us cfr)
description: Alcoholic or nonalcoholic beverage; excludes milk and milk-based beverages, fruit juices and fruit juice drinks, and vegetable juices. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

name: nut or nut product (us cfr)
description: Nuts in all forms, including nut butters and pastes.

name: seafood or seafood product (us cfr)
description: Flesh from fish or shellfish. Includes seafood product analogs and seafood-based sausage or luncheon meat as well as such products as squid ink and clam juice.

name: USA agency food product type
description: Food group having common consumption, functional or manufacturing characteristics, e.g. *FRUIT OR VEGETABLE PRODUCT*, *DAIRY PRODUCT*, *CONFECTIONARY*, *PREPARED FOOD PRODUCT*, etc. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

name: international agency food product type
description: Renamed from *PRODUCT TYPE, CODEX ALIMENTARIUS* in LanguaL 2008.

name: agency food product type
description: An agency food product type is a class of food product defined by an agency or consortium.

name: Codex Alimentarius classification of food and feed commodities
description: Codex Alimentarius, Volume 2 - 1993, Section 2:  Pesticide Residues in Food.  The Codex Classification of food and animal feed commodities moving in trade and the description of the various items and groups of food and animal feedstuffs included in the present document have been developed by the Codex Committee on Pesticide Residues. It was first adopted by the 18th Session of the Codex Alimentarius Commission, (1989).  The Codex Classification includes food commodities and animal feedstuffs for which Codex maximum residue limits will not necessarily be established. The Classification is intended to be as complete a listing of food commodities in trade as possible, classified into groups on the basis of the commodity's similar potential for pesticide residues.  The Classification may also be appropriate for other purposes such as setting maximum levels for other types of residues or for other contaminants in food. The Codex Classification should be consulted in order to obtain a precise description of the food or animal feed commodities and, especially, in cases where Codex maximum residue limits have been set for groups of food and groups of animal feedstuffs. The Codex Classification is intended to promote harmonization of the terms used to describe commodities which are subject to maximum residue limits and of the approach to grouping commodities with similar potential for residue for which a common group maximum residue limit can be set.

name: a.  primary food commodities of plant origin (ccpr)
04  nuts and seeds (ccpr)
description: TYPE 04  -  NUTS AND SEEDS  Nuts and seeds are derived from a large variety of trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants, mostly cultivated.  The mature seeds or nuts are used as human food, for the production of beverages or edible vegetable oils and for the production of seed meals and cakes for animal feed.

name: 022  tree nuts (tn) (ccpr)
description: Tree nuts are the seeds of a variety of trees and shrubs which are characterized by a hard inedible shell enclosing an oily seed. The seed is protected from pesticides applied during the growing season by the shell and other parts of the fruit. The edible portion of the nut is consumed in succulent, dried or processed forms.

name: U.S. code of federal regulations, title 21 food product type
description: Food and Drugs, title 21, Code of Federal Regulations. Original food classification in LanguaL.

name: plant used for producing extract or concentrate
fish or lower water animal
description: An aquatic animal is an animal, either vertebrate or invertebrate, which lives in the water for most or all of its lifetime.

name: chemical food component
description: Any chemical or chemical mixture that exists in a food material or was added to a food material.

name: shellfish or crustacean
description: Shellfish is a food source and fisheries term for exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates used as food, including various species of molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms. Although most kinds of shellfish are harvested from saltwater environments, some kinds are found in freshwater. In addition, a few species of land crabs are eaten, for example *Cardisoma guanhumi* in the Caribbean. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shellfish]

name: penaeid shrimp family
description: *Penaeidae* is a family of marine crustacean in the suborder *Dendrobranchiata*, which are often referred to as penaeid shrimp or penaeid prawn. It contains many species of economic importance, such as the tiger prawn, whiteleg shrimp, Atlantic white shrimp and Indian prawn. Many prawns are the subject of commercial fishery, and farming, both in marine settings, and in freshwater farms. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penaeidae]

name: mammal
description: Mammals (from Latin mamma "breast") are vertebrate animals constituting the class Mammalia, and characterized by the presence of mammary glands which in females produce milk for feeding (nursing) their young, a neocortex (a region of the brain), fur or hair, and three middle ear bones.

name: aquatic invertebrate animal (excluding shellfish)
description: Aquatic animals other than fish and shellfish

name: dairy cow
description: A dairy cow is an adult female member of a dairy cattle breed

name: fish
description: A gill-bearing aquatic craniate animal that lacks limbs with digits.

name: shrimp
description: A whole shrimp.

name: fungus
description: A member of the group of eukaryotic organisms in the kingdom Fungi that includes unicellular microorganisms such as yeasts and molds, as well as multicellular fungi that produce familiar fruiting forms known as mushrooms.

name: vertebrate animal
description: A vertebrate animal is any species of organism within the subphylum Vertebrata (chordates with backbones). Vertebrates represent the overwhelming majority of the phylum Chordata, with currently about 69,276 species described.

name: algae
description: An informal term for a large, diverse group of photosynthetic eukaryotic organisms that are not necessarily closely related, and is thus polyphyletic.

name: wheat plant
description: Wheat (*Triticum* spp.) is a domesticated grass from the Levant that is cultivated worldwide. Major cultivated species of wheat:      * Common wheat or Bread wheat (*Triticum aestivum*) A hexaploid species that is the most widely cultivated in the world.      * Durum (*Triticum durum*) The only tetraploid form of wheat widely used today, and the second most widely cultivated wheat.      * Einkorn (*Triticum monococcum*) A diploid species with wild and cultivated variants. Domesticated at the same time as emmer wheat, but never reached the same importance.      * Emmer (*Triticum dicoccon*) A tetraploid species, cultivated in ancient times but no longer in widespread use.      * Spelt (*Triticum spelta*) Another hexaploid species cultivated in limited quantities.

name: grain plant
description: Any grass cultivated (grown) for the edible components of its grain.

name: goat
description: A whole goat.

name: crustacean
description: Crustaceans form a large, diverse arthropod taxon which includes such familiar animals as crabs, lobsters, crayfish, shrimp, krill, woodlice, and barnacles. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean]

name: shellfish
description: The term shellfish is used both broadly and specifically. For regulatory purposes it is often narrowly defined as filter-feeding molluscs such as clams, mussels, and oyster to the exclusion of crustaceans and all else. Although their shells may differ, all shellfish are invertebrates.

name: organism by alternate grouping
description: This is a hierarchy of organisms, grouped minimally in a combination of taxonomy and consumer-oriented food groups.

name: nut or edible seed producing plant
decapod
description: The Decapoda or decapods (literally "ten-footed") are an order of crustaceans within the class Malacostraca, including many familiar groups, such as crayfish, crabs, lobsters, prawns, and shrimp. Most decapods are scavengers. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decapoda]

name: mollusc
description: *Mollusca* is a large phylum of invertebrate animals whose members are known as molluscs or mollusks. Molluscs are the largest marine phylum, comprising about 23% of all the named marine organisms. Numerous molluscs also live in freshwater and terrestrial habitats. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusca]

name: echinoderm
description: Echinoderm is the common name given to any member of the phylum *Echinodermata* of marine animals. The adults are recognizable by their (usually five-point) radial symmetry, and include such well-known animals as sea stars, sea urchins, sand dollars, and sea cucumbers, as well as the sea lilies or "stone lilies". [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinoderm]

name: mud crab family
description: Mud crab may refer to any crab that lives in or near mud, such as: species from family *Portunidae*, such as *Scylla serrata*; *Scylla tranquebarica*; *Scylla paramamosain*; members of the family *Panopeidae*, such as *Panopeus herbstii*; members of the family *Xanthidae*; *Helice crassa*, the tunnelling mud crab. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mud_crab]

name: lichen
description: A composite organism that arises from algae or cyanobacteria living among filaments of multiple fungi species in a mutualistic relationship.

name: coelenterate
description: *Coelenterata* is an obsolete term encompassing the animal phyla *Cnidaria* (coral animals, true jellies, sea anemones, sea pens, and their allies) and *Ctenophora* (comb jellies).  [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coelenterata]

name: doe (goat)
description: A female goat

name: kid (goat)
description: A young goat

name: bovine
description: The biological subfamily *Bovinae* includes a diverse group of 10 genera of medium- to large-sized ungulates, including domestic cattle, the bison, African buffalo, the water buffalo, the yak, and the four-horned and spiral-horned antelopes. The evolutionary relationship between the members of the group is obscure, and their classification into loose tribes rather than formal subgroups reflects this uncertainty. General characteristics include cloven hoofs and usually at least one of the sexes of a species having true horns.

name: bovid
description: A bovid (family *Bovidae*) is any of almost 140 species of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammal which has males with characteristic unbranching horns covered in a permanent sheath of keratin.  The family is widespread, being native to Asia, Africa, Europe and North America, and diverse: members include bison, African buffalo, water buffalo, antelopes, gazelles, sheep, goats, muskoxen, and domestic cattle.

name: tunicate
description: Tunicates, previously known as *Urochordata* or urochordates, are members of the *Tunicata*, a subphylum of the phylum *Chordata*. They are marine filter feeders with a saclike morphology. In their respiration and feeding they take in water through an incurrent (or inhalant) siphon and expel the filtered water through an excurrent (or exhalant) siphon. Most adult tunicates are sessile and attached to rocks or similarly suitable surfaces on the ocean floor; others such as salps, doliolids and pyrosomes swim in the pelagic zone as adults. Various species are commonly known as sea squirts or sea pork.

name: mammalian milk or milk component
description: A broad term that includes milk and its components, cream, curd and whey; use the appropriate specific term when milk or a milk product is the principal ingredient. Use the appropriate term under *MEAT ANIMAL* to index the source of the milk (note: 21 CFR 131.110 defines milk as cow's milk).

name: organism material
description: Anatomical or other part(s) or substances derived from plant or animal or fungal organisms.

name: nonmeat part of animal
description: Bone, feathers, shell, skin or trim fat.

name: plant above surface, excluding fruit and seed
root, stem, leaf or flower
description: The parts of a plant that are not fruit or seed.

name: animal material
description: Material that derives from some animal.

name: fruit part
description: The fleshy fruit of any plant. *FRUIT* includes vegetables berries and pods as well. The bulk of a fruit is its fleshy part, which is covered by a peel (skin) and which encloses a core, pit or seeds.

name: bone or shell
description: Bone (endoskeleton) or shell (exoskeleton) of animals, or any part thereof.

name: obsolete: part of plant
description: Anatomical part of a plant, such as fruit, seed, pod, leaf, stem or flower as well as the whole plant.

name: gluten
description: Extract, concentrate or isolate high in gluten, the predominant protein of wheat or corn.

name: egg or egg component
description: Poultry, game bird or turtle eggs.

name: extract, concentrate or isolate of plant or animal
description: A physical-chemical component separated from the food source or its parts by extraction, centrifugation, filtration, heat processing, expressing or a similar process. The separated component may be converted through further processing. If this is done, the final substance is indexed. A water-extracted component may remain in aqueous dispersion. The extract, concentrate or isolate is indexed in preference to the anatomic part from which it is derived. For example, peanut oil is indexed under *PEANUT* combined wih *FAT OR OIL* rather than with *SEED OR KERNEL*. On the other hand, fruit and vegetable juices can be indexed under *FRUIT JUICE OR NECTAR* or *VEGETABLE JUICE* (A. PRODUCT TYPE); therefore the anatomic part of the plant should be indexed.

name: protein extract, concentrate or isolate
description: Extract, concentrate or isolate high in protein; may contain amino acids, polypeptides and enzymes.

name: floret or flower
description: The pigmented blossom of a plant that contains the reproductive  organs; a floret is a single flower of a multiple flowered inflorescence. Also includes flower buds.

name: fruit core (anatomical part)
description: The hard, central part of an apple, pear, etc., that contains the seeds (Source: Webster's)

name: fruit peel (anatomical part)
description: The rind or skin of fruit

name: fruit seed (anatomical part)
description: The part of a flowering plant that typically contains the embryo with its protective coat and stored food and that can develop into a new plant under the proper conditions; fertilised and mature ovule (Source: Webster's).  Seeds and fruits commonly called seeds include: grain, kernel, berry, ear, corn, nut. (Source: Webster's Thesaurus).

name: food (liquid, high viscosity)
description: A liquid that flows slowly at room temperature. Examples are: some heavy liqueurs, evaporated milk, vegetable oil, molasses and honey. The range of high viscosity liquids spans sucrose solutions between 45 and 70% solids (viscosity range from 10 to 500 centipoise). Prefer 'solid pieces' factor term to 'small particles' if both appear in the food.

name: food (liquid, low viscosity)
description: A liquid that flows very easily at room temperature. Examples are: water, apple juice, sherry, acidophilus milk, whipping cream and some heavy liqueurs. The range of low viscosity liquid spans sucrose solutions between 0 and 45% solids (viscosity range from 1 to 10 centipoise). Prefer 'solid pieces' factor term to 'small particles' if both appear in the food.

name: food physical quality
description: The physical state of the food product (liquid, semiliquid, semisolid, or solid). Solid food products are further subdivided by shape or form. Terms are provided for products that have both liquid and solid components or that incorporate air or other gases. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

name: food (liquid)
description: A state of matter between a solid and a gas, in which a substance has the capacity to flow and conforms to the shape of the container. Liquids range from water to honey, corresponding to a range in viscosity (or apparent viscosity) from 1 to 500 centipoise (viscosity is a measure of a liquid's resistance to flow). Products that are pourable but have a higher viscosity are *SEMILIQUID*.

name: whole
description: Refers to natural or formed shape as appropriate, regardless of size, which may vary from very large (e.g., beef carcass) to very small (e.g., poppy seed, yeast cell).

name: food (solid)
description: A solid product is a hard or soft product capable of retaining its own shape at room temperature (20 degrees C.). A soft product that is spreadable or formable is considered semisolid.

name: food treatment process
description: Used to specifically characterize a food product based on the treatment or processes applied to the product or any indexed ingredient. The processes include adding, substituting or removing components or modifying the food or component, e.g., through fermentation.

name: microbial/enzymatic modification process
description: A food modification process by microbial or enzymatic action which results in molecular changes in any food component.

name: physical/chemical modification process
description: A food modification process where physical or chemical changes are effected in any food ingredient through a physical or non-enzymatic chemical process.

name: plant seed or nut food product
food preservation process
description: The methods contributing to the prevention or retardation of microbial, enzymatic or oxidative spoilage and thus to the extension of shelf life. Index all methods for which information is available, even if a corresponding descriptor has already been used in *H. TREATMENT APPLIED*. Preservation descriptors refer to the finished food as a whole with these exceptions: (1) if the components of a multi-component food, such as cream pie, are preservation by different methods, index all methods; (2)  if chemical preservatives are declared on the label, always index them even if it is known that the preservative was introduced through or is only present in a component or ingredient of the food; and (3) if the preservation method for an ingredient is declared on the label (such as brie cheese made from pasteurized milk) index it. Also use *INGREDIENT preservation by THERMAL PROCESSING* or *INGREDIENT preservation by IRRADIATION* when ingredients have been pasteurized, ultrapasteurized, sterilized or irradiated.

name: food consumer group
description: A food consumer group is a class of organism based on their heterotrophic requirements or preferences.

name: Restlessness
description: A state of unease is characterized by diffuse motor activity or motion, which is subject to limited control, nonproductive, or disorganized behavior.

name: Agitation
description: A state of excessive motor activity that is associated with mental distress or a feeling of substantial unease or inner tension. Distinguished from restlessness by the increased level of emotional distress and negative intensity of the experience. Agitation has a significant level of physical activity that is typically threatening to the self or others.

name: Aggressive behavior
description: Behavior or an act aimed at harming a person, animal, or physical property (e.g., acts of physical violence; shouting, swearing, and using harsh language; slashing someone's tires).

name: Inappropriate behavior
description: An explicit or perceived action, demonstration, conduct, or language (verbal and written) that is contrary to generally accepted norms, rules, procedures, or unacceptable within the context in which it is carried out. Inappropriate behaviors could take place in a sexual or social context and could be aggressive, violent, impulsive, intimidating, or threatening in nature.

name: Compulsive behaviors
description: Behavior that consists of repetitive acts, characterized by the feeling that one "has to" perform them, while being aware that these acts are not in line with one's overall goal.

name: Disinhibition
description: Reduced ability to control, or a failure to resist a temptation, urge, or impulse. Examples include disregard for social conventions, general impulsivity, and poor risk assessment.

name: Irritability
description: A proneness to anger, i.e., a tendency to become easily bothered or annoyed.

name: Anxiety
description: Intense feelings of nervousness, tension, or panic often arise in response to interpersonal stresses. There is worry about the negative effects of past unpleasant experiences and future negative possibilities. Individuals may feel fearful, apprehensive, or threatened by uncertainty, and they may also have fears of falling apart or losing control.

name: Apathy
description: Apathy is a quantitative reduction of interest, motivation and the initiation and persistence of goal-directed behavior, where often the accompanying emotions, thoughts, and social interactions are also diminished. The individual is typically non-reactive to provocations, positive or negative, and appears to not care. Distinguished from lethargy which involves lack of physical or mental energy.

name: Abnormal diminished volition
